Accountable obligation owner.value: Head of IT owns the configuration baseline that enforces the Cyber Code's 14-day BMA notification clock and notice content rules; Configuration Engineer performs, Chief Info Security Officer accepts as second line

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Bermuda Insurance Sector Operational Cyber Risk Management Code of Conduct (2020), 3LOD and governance paragraphs, re-read on the BMA website at each configuration change; the 14-day incident notification window is transcribed verbatim into the rule spec

In-scope processes.value: Cyber incident detection → triage → BMA notification, and the change-control process governing every administrative system setting that drives notification timing, mandatory notice content or three-lines-of-defence entitlement separation

In-scope systems.value: ITSM incident record type and SLA clocks, Splunk SIEM detection-to-case handoff, GRC obligation register, and IAM entitlement roles for first/second/third line

Compliance procedure documented.value: Cyber Notification Configuration Standard — rule spec authoring, config build, non-production scenario test, second-line peer review, CAB approval, post-implementation verification, evidence pack

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and the Head of IT; re-approved on every BMA cyber guidance update and at least annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change — the configuration must be live before the change window closes; the rule it enforces is the 14-day BMA notification deadline measured from the incident being assessed as material, plus the 14-day follow-up after the initial notification

Deadline reminders configured.value: ITSM escalation jobs fire at day 3, day 7, day 10 and day 13 of the 14-day clock to the incident owner, Chief Info Security Officer and Compliance Officer; a day-13 breach page goes to the Head of IT

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Rule spec, config export, non-production test results, peer review note, CAB record and post-implementation screenshots retained 7 years from the date the configuration is superseded

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any production configuration drift that disables an SLA clock, a mandatory field or a segregation rule is raised as a control exception with root cause, compensating control and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CISO signs off every configuration that touches the notification clock or 3LOD entitlements, and every drift remediation before the exception is closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All change records in the period that altered incident record types, SLA clocks, notification templates, mandatory fields or 3LOD entitlement roles, plus every cyber incident raised in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on the 14-day clock — any incident whose clock was mis-configured or silently stopped is a fail; ≥1 unapproved production config change or any first-line user holding a third-line approval entitlement is a fail escalated to the Chief Info Security Officer

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change; testing runs quarterly over that quarter's change population with 100% coverage of changes touching the notification clock, and annually as a full baseline re-performance

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must hold no write access to the ITSM or IAM configuration and must not have built or approved any sampled change

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly cyber-configuration test workpaper (change extract, sample, config re-performance screenshots, clock recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Cyber Code / 3LOD

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Configuration baseline document, change history export and the notification timeline for each incident, producible for a BMA on-site review within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Chief Info Security Officer is the named BMA contact for cyber matters; Compliance Officer files the notification through the BMA electronic filing channel and General Counsel clears any statement admitting a missed 14-day notification

checklist.step: Take in the change request and name the Code paragraph it enforces
actions: Open Change ▸ New Normal Change and set Category = 'Regulatory configuration', Configuration Item = the incident management application.
In the Justification field paste the Cyber Code paragraph being enforced (3LOD role separation, governance reporting, or the 14-day notification window) and the BMA document date (2020).
Ask the Compliance Officer to confirm in the change record whether the setting affects a notification deadline, notice content, or an entitlement — that answer sets the approval path.
Attach the current production configuration export as the 'before' state.
checklist.done: the change record names the Code paragraph, the affected setting class and carries a before-state export.

checklist.step: Translate the 14-day notification rule into a machine-readable rule spec
actions: Create a rule spec page and write the clock definition: start = timestamp the incident is assessed material by the Incident Response Lead; stop = timestamp the BMA notification is submitted; duration = 14 calendar days, not business days.
Define the follow-up rule separately: a further report is due within 14 days of the initial notification.
State the calendar convention explicitly (calendar days, Atlantic time zone, no suspension for weekends or Bermuda public holidays).
Have the Compliance Officer sign the spec page before any build starts, and record the sign-off date.
checklist.done: a signed rule spec states the clock start event, stop event, 14-day duration and calendar convention in unambiguous terms.

checklist.step: Draft the mandatory content template for the BMA notification
actions: List the fields the BMA expects in a cyber incident notification: entity name and registration number, date and time of discovery, date assessed material, incident type, systems and data affected, policyholder impact, containment actions, third parties involved and remediation plan.
Mark each field mandatory or conditional and give each one a validation rule (date not in the future, free text minimum 100 characters, impact count numeric).
Write the notification narrative template with placeholders for every mandatory field.
Hand the template and field list to the Configuration Engineer as the build input and file it with the rule spec.
checklist.done: a field-by-field content template exists with mandatory flags and validation rules for every field.

checklist.step: Configure the incident record type and the 14-day SLA clock
actions: In the ITSM admin console open Service Level Management ▸ SLA Definitions and create 'BMA Cyber Notification — 14 calendar days'.
Set the start condition to the 'Materiality assessed = Yes' field transition and the stop condition to 'BMA notification submitted = true'; leave the schedule as 24x7 so weekends are counted.
Create a second SLA 'BMA Follow-up Report — 14 days' starting on the initial notification timestamp.
Disable manual pause on both SLAs so no analyst can stop the clock, and record the setting in the change record.
Export the SLA definition to the change record as the 'after' state.
checklist.done: both SLAs exist, run on a 24x7 calendar, cannot be paused manually, and are exported into the change record.

checklist.step: Wire the SIEM detection so the discovery timestamp cannot be back-dated
actions: In Splunk open Enterprise Security ▸ Incident Review and configure the notable-event adaptive response action that opens the ITSM incident.
Map the notable event's first-seen _time into the ITSM 'Detected at' field as read-only so analysts cannot edit it.
Configure the correlation searches covering the in-scope cyber use cases to raise notables at urgency High or above.
Run a synthetic notable and confirm the ITSM record inherits the SIEM timestamp unaltered.
Hand the synthetic test output to the Configuration Engineer for the evidence pack.
checklist.done: SIEM-originated incidents carry a read-only detection timestamp proven by a synthetic notable end-to-end test.

checklist.step: Register the obligation and its control mapping in the GRC platform
actions: Open Policy and Compliance ▸ Authority Documents and create or update the entry for the Bermuda Insurance Sector Operational Cyber Risk Management Code of Conduct (2020).
Create citations for the 3LOD paragraph, the governance paragraph and the 14-day notification requirement.
Link each citation to the configured controls: SLA clock, mandatory-field validation, entitlement segregation and escalation jobs.
Set the control owner to the Head of IT, the control tester to Internal Audit and the review frequency to quarterly.
checklist.done: each cited Code paragraph is mapped to a named configured control with an owner and a test frequency.

checklist.step: Enforce three-lines-of-defence separation in the entitlement model
actions: Create three ITSM roles: cyber_first_line_operate, cyber_second_line_review and cyber_third_line_assure, with review and assurance rights held only by the latter two.
In the IAM platform define separation-of-duty policies that block any identity holding first-line operate together with second-line review or third-line assurance.
Run the policy in simulation across current entitlements and export the violation list.
Send the violation list to the Chief Info Security Officer for revocation decisions and revoke within the same change window.
Enable the policy in enforcing mode and set the certification campaign to quarterly.
checklist.done: separation-of-duty policies are enforcing, simulated violations are revoked, and a quarterly certification campaign is scheduled.

checklist.step: Configure mandatory fields and content blocks so an incomplete notice cannot be issued
actions: In Form Designer add the notification fields from the content template to the cyber incident form.
Add UI policies making each mandatory field required when 'Materiality assessed = Yes'.
Add a client script blocking the 'Submit BMA notification' button while any mandatory field is empty or fails its validation rule.
Load the approved narrative template as the notification body with placeholders bound to the fields, so no free-typed notice can be sent.
Screenshot the blocked-submit behaviour in the sandbox for the evidence pack.
checklist.done: the submit action is technically blocked until every mandatory notification field passes validation, evidenced by a sandbox screenshot.

checklist.step: Configure the day 3 / 7 / 10 / 13 escalation jobs
actions: Under the BMA Cyber Notification SLA add escalation events at 21%, 50%, 71% and 93% elapsed — day 3, 7, 10 and 13 of the 14-day window.
Route day 3 and 7 to the incident owner and Incident Response Lead, day 10 to the Chief Info Security Officer, day 13 to the Head of IT and the Compliance Officer.
Set the notification channel to email plus an on-call page for the day 13 event.
Trigger each escalation in the sandbox with a back-dated test incident and capture the resulting messages.
checklist.done: all four escalations fire at the intended elapsed points with the intended recipients, proven in the sandbox.

checklist.step: Lock the audit trail and retention on incidents and notifications
actions: Configure the ITSM audit history on the cyber incident table to record field-level changes to the materiality flag, the detection timestamp and the notification submission timestamp.
Set the archival job to export closed cyber incidents plus the notification PDF into the compliance evidence repository weekly.
Apply a 7-year retention label measured from the date the configuration or incident is superseded or closed.
Confirm the repository index makes records searchable by incident number, discovery date and notification date.
checklist.done: field-level audit history is on, weekly archival runs, and records carry a 7-year label and are searchable by incident and notification date.

checklist.step: Run dated scenario tests in the non-production environment
actions: Build four scenarios: materiality assessed on a Friday, on a Bermuda public holiday, an incident escalated to material five days after detection, and an incident notified on day 14.
For each scenario record the expected due date computed by hand from the rule spec and the due date the system displays.
Attempt to submit each notification with one mandatory field blank and confirm the submit is refused.
Attempt to pause the SLA as a first-line user and confirm it is refused.
Log every scenario, expected result and actual result in the test evidence sheet.
checklist.done: all four scenarios show the system due date equal to the hand-computed due date, and both negative tests are refused.

checklist.step: Second-line peer review of the configuration against the rule spec
actions: Read the rule spec and the config export side by side without the builder present.
Confirm the clock schedule is 24x7, pause is disabled, and the start/stop conditions match the spec field for field.
Confirm the entitlement separation policy is in enforcing, not simulation, mode.
Record confirm or reject on the change record; a reject returns the change to the Configuration Engineer and cannot be overridden by the first line.
checklist.done: a dated second-line review decision sits on the change record and no rejected item is promoted.

checklist.step: Obtain CAB approval and schedule the release window
actions: Table the change at the Change Advisory Board with the rule spec, sandbox test evidence and second-line review note attached.
Record the CISO approval as a mandatory approver on the change record for any clock or entitlement setting.
Set the implementation window and a documented back-out plan naming the config export to restore.
Set the post-implementation review task to run within 24 hours of promotion.
checklist.done: the change is CAB-approved with CISO approval recorded, a back-out export named and a PIR task scheduled.

checklist.step: Promote to production and verify the settings survived the release
actions: Promote the update set in the approved window and confirm zero collisions or skipped records in the preview log.
In production open the SLA definition and confirm the 14-day duration, 24x7 schedule and disabled manual pause.
Raise a live low-severity test incident, mark it material, read the displayed due date and confirm it is exactly 14 calendar days out, then cancel it.
Confirm the four escalation events are listed as active against the SLA.
checklist.done: production shows the intended SLA, escalations and validation behaviour, verified on a live test incident inside 24 hours.

checklist.step: File the configuration evidence pack against the obligation
actions: Assemble the pack: rule spec, content template, before/after config exports, SIEM synthetic test output, IAM separation policy export, sandbox scenario sheet, second-line review, CAB record and PIR screenshots.
File it under Cyber Code / 3LOD with the change number and the go-live date in the record title.
Link the pack to the GRC control record so the tester finds it without asking.
Apply the 7-year retention label and close the change record.
checklist.done: a single linked evidence pack exists per configuration change, labelled for 7-year retention and reachable from the GRC control.

testing.step: Build the population of configuration changes and cyber incidents for the quarter
actions: Export all change records in the quarter where the configuration item is the incident management application, the SIEM, or the IAM entitlement model.
Export all cyber incidents raised in the quarter with their materiality flag, detection timestamp, materiality timestamp and notification timestamp.
Add emergency and standard changes so out-of-CAB fixes cannot hide in the population.
Have the extractor sign the extract with the query, run date and record counts.
testing.done: both populations are extracted with query, run date and counts, and signed by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the change population to the source of record
actions: Compare the ITSM change count to the platform's own configuration audit log of applied update sets for the same dates.
Investigate every applied update set with no matching change record and list it as an unauthorised change candidate.
Compare the incident population to the SIEM notable-event count at urgency High or above and explain every gap.
Resolve or document every difference before drawing the sample.
testing.done: the change and incident populations reconcile to the platform audit log and SIEM counts, with every difference explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of changes touching the 14-day SLA clock, the mandatory-field validation or the 3LOD entitlement policy.
Take 20 further changes selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population.
Take 100% of incidents flagged material and 15 non-material incidents at random.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible from the recorded seed, and covers every clock and entitlement change.

testing.step: Re-perform the clock configuration directly in the production console
actions: Open Service Level Management ▸ SLA Definitions in production with read-only rights and read the BMA Cyber Notification definition.
Confirm duration = 14 days, schedule = 24x7, manual pause disabled, start condition = materiality flag transition, stop condition = notification submitted.
Reach your own conclusion before reading the rule spec, then compare; any difference — including a right duration on a business-day calendar — is an exception.
Screenshot the definition into the workpaper with the read date.
testing.done: an independent read of the production SLA definition is captured and compared field by field to the signed rule spec.

testing.step: Recompute the 14-day notification maths on every material incident
actions: For each material incident, recompute due date = materiality assessment timestamp + 14 calendar days by hand in the workpaper.
Compare to the system-displayed due date and to the actual BMA notification submission timestamp.
Recompute the follow-up report due date as initial notification + 14 days and check it was met.
Treat any notification after the recomputed due date as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every material incident has a hand-recomputed due date reconciled to the system date and the actual submission date.

testing.step: Test the mandatory-content enforcement by attempting a deficient submission
actions: In the audit test instance raise an incident, mark it material and leave the 'date assessed material' and 'systems affected' fields blank.
Attempt to press 'Submit BMA notification' and record whether the action is refused with a field-level message.
Enter a future-dated discovery date and confirm the validation rejects it.
Open five sampled real notifications and confirm every mandatory field from the content template is populated with substantive text, not placeholders.
testing.done: deficient submissions are refused in a live test and five real notifications carry substantive values in every mandatory field.

testing.step: Test three-lines-of-defence entitlement separation against the actual user base
actions: Export the current membership of cyber_first_line_operate, cyber_second_line_review and cyber_third_line_assure.
Intersect the three lists and list every identity appearing in more than one, including service and break-glass accounts.
Confirm the separation-of-duty policy is in enforcing mode and read its last certification campaign completion date.
For each sampled second-line review record, confirm the reviewer is not the builder named on the change.
testing.done: no identity holds conflicting line entitlements without a documented, CISO-approved exception, and no reviewer reviewed their own build.

testing.step: Trace each sampled change to its full evidence pack and approvals
actions: For each sampled change open the linked evidence pack and confirm the rule spec, sandbox scenario sheet, second-line review, CAB record and PIR screenshots are all present and dated.
Check every approval date pre-dates the promotion timestamp — approvals recorded after go-live are exceptions.
Confirm the retention label is applied and the pack is reachable from the GRC control record.
List any pack missing an artefact with the specific artefact named.
testing.done: every sampled change has a complete, pre-dated evidence pack linked from its GRC control, or the missing artefact is named.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the change or incident number, the setting affected and the compliance impact on the 14-day obligation.
Assign a root cause from the agreed taxonomy: spec not updated, config drift, unapproved emergency change, entitlement creep, or calendar misconfiguration.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for any missed notification open a self-report assessment with General Counsel and the Chief Info Security Officer.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, a taxonomy root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance clock threshold and the entitlement conflict count.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper reference behind each element.
Have the reviewer, who holds no write access to the ITSM or IAM configuration, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any missed notification to the Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an exception rate, a stated conclusion and a Risk Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Compliance Manager owns the annual fair-treatment curriculum and the completion result; Learning & Development Specialist builds and deploys it, Head of Compliance reports the outcome to the board

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Bermuda Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022), business conduct and integrity paragraphs plus the consequences-of-non-compliance paragraph, re-read against the BMA-published PDF each year before the curriculum is refreshed

In-scope processes.value: Product design sign-off, sales and distribution conduct, and claims handling — every process where a policyholder is treated fairly or is not; plus new-joiner onboarding and role-change reassignment

In-scope systems.value: Course build, assignment and completion tracking in the LMS, with the audience fed nightly from the HRIS worker feed

Compliance procedure documented.value: Fair Treatment of Policyholders Training Procedure — audience definition, content mapping to Code paragraphs, 80% pass mark, 30-day completion window, escalation ladder, record retention

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and noted by the Compliance Committee; content re-approved annually and within 90 days of any BMA Code amendment

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual cycle — assignment on 1 October, completion due 30 November, board reporting at the December Compliance Committee; new joiners due within 30 days of hire date; role changers within 30 days of the effective transfer date

Deadline reminders configured.value: LMS automated reminders at day 7, day 21 and day 28 of the 30-day window, then a weekly line-manager exception list from 1 November and a day-45 escalation to the department head

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Course content version, assessment questions and scores, completion certificates and the exception log retained 7 years from the training year, exportable per employee

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every non-completer past day 45 is logged with the reason (leave of absence, secondment, refusal), the compensating restriction applied, and the disposition decided by the Head of Compliance

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs the year-end completion attestation and personally approves any waiver or extension beyond day 45

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All active employees and contingent workers in claims, sales, distribution, product and complaints roles per the HRIS worker list at 30 November, plus every joiner and role changer during the year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% completion for in-scope staff by 30 November with an assessment score of at least 80%; any completion recorded without an assessment attempt, or any staff member handling claims without training, is an automatic fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the completion test runs once in December over the full year population, with a mid-year interim test in June covering joiners only

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance and Learning & Development and must not have authored or delivered any sampled course

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual fair-treatment training test workpaper (HRIS population extract, LMS completion export, reconciliation, sample of scores, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Insurance Code of Conduct / business conduct

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Curriculum-to-Code mapping table, course content PDF, per-employee completion register and the Head of Compliance attestation, producible for a BMA review or a market conduct examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance answers BMA questions on conduct training; Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager handles examiner requests for training records; General Counsel clears any response disclosing a training shortfall

checklist.step: Define the in-scope audience from the HRIS worker list
actions: Run the Workers report filtered to job families Claims, Sales and Distribution, Product Development, Complaints and Contact Centre, including contingent workers.
Add every people manager above those populations regardless of job family.
Export employee id, legal name, job profile, cost centre, manager, hire date and work country.
Send the list to the Compliance Manager and agree exclusions in writing — an exclusion with no written reason is not an exclusion.
checklist.done: a dated audience extract exists with per-employee attributes and a written, agreed exclusion list.

checklist.step: Map the curriculum to the Code paragraphs it must cover
actions: Open the Bermuda Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) PDF and list the business-conduct and integrity obligations sentence by sentence.
Build a mapping table with one row per obligation: Code paragraph, plain-English behaviour expected, the process it lands in (product design, sales, claims), and the module that will teach it.
Add a row for the consequences-of-non-compliance paragraph so staff are taught what the BMA can do.
Have the Compliance Manager confirm no obligation row is left without a module.
checklist.done: every business-conduct obligation in the Code maps to a named module, confirmed by the Compliance Manager.

checklist.step: Build the course content around real claims and sales scenarios
actions: Write four scenario modules: a suitability-poor annuity sale, a claim denied on a technicality, a product feature that is hard for the policyholder to understand, and a vulnerable-customer complaint.
For each scenario show the wrong handling, the Code paragraph it breaches, and the expected handling with the internal escalation route.
Ask the Complaints Manager for two anonymised complaints from the past year and build them in as case studies.
Write a 15-question assessment with an 80% pass mark and randomised question order, at least two questions per module.
Set the course to require the assessment before completion is recorded.
checklist.done: the course carries four scenario modules drawn from real complaints and an 80% pass-mark assessment that gates completion.

checklist.step: Obtain compliance and business sign-off on the content before release
actions: Review the mapping table and the course build against the current Code text.
Have the Chief Claims Officer and the Head of Distribution confirm the claims and sales scenarios match how their teams actually operate.
Record the approval with the content version number and the approval date on the course record.
Reject and return any module that teaches process without naming the Code obligation behind it.
checklist.done: the content version is approved by Compliance, Claims and Distribution with a dated record on the course.

checklist.step: Load the course and configure the assignment rules
actions: Publish the course under the Compliance catalogue as 'Fair Treatment of Policyholders — Insurance Code of Conduct <year>'.
Create a dynamic learner group fed from the HRIS job-family attributes so joiners are picked up nightly without manual action.
Set the assignment date to 1 October, the due date to 30 November, and a 30-day due date for anyone added after 1 October.
Configure reminder emails at day 7, day 21 and day 28 and a manager copy on the day 28 reminder.
Run a test assignment on a sandbox learner and confirm the due-date maths and reminders.
checklist.done: the course is published, the dynamic group is live from HRIS, and due dates and reminders are proven on a test learner.

checklist.step: Announce the campaign and brief people managers
actions: Send the launch email on 1 October naming the 30 November deadline, the 80% pass mark and the consequence of non-completion.
Give each people manager a link to their team's completion dashboard and the escalation timetable.
Post the course link in the Claims, Distribution and Contact Centre Teams channels.
Diary the reminder communications for 1 November and 20 November.
checklist.done: launch and reminder communications are scheduled and every people manager holds a dashboard link and the escalation timetable.

checklist.step: Deliver facilitated sessions for claims and sales front-line teams
actions: Schedule live sessions per shift pattern so contact centre and claims staff can attend without dropping service levels — agree the slots with the Contact Center Ops Manager.
Work the four scenarios live and capture attendee questions that show a policy gap.
Record attendance against employee id and load it to the LMS as a completion component, not as a substitute for the assessment.
Send unanswered questions to the Compliance Analyst for a written FAQ within 5 business days.
checklist.done: sessions are delivered per shift, attendance is recorded against employee ids, and open questions have a written FAQ answer.

checklist.step: Cover new joiners inside 30 days of hire
actions: Confirm the onboarding checklist includes the fair-treatment course as a mandatory day-one task for in-scope job families.
Run a weekly report of hires in the last 7 days and check each one appears in the LMS dynamic group.
Manually assign anyone the nightly feed missed and note why the feed missed them.
Report any joiner past day 30 without completion to the Compliance Manager the same week.
checklist.done: every in-scope joiner is assigned within one week of hire and non-completers past day 30 are reported weekly.

checklist.step: Reassign training on role changes into in-scope job families
actions: Run the monthly Job Change report and identify moves into Claims, Sales, Distribution, Product or Complaints.
Check whether the mover completed the current-year course; where not, confirm the LMS assigned it with a 30-day due date from the transfer effective date.
Remove leavers and movers out of scope from open assignments so the completion denominator stays honest.
Send the monthly movement reconciliation to the Learning Development Manager.
checklist.done: every in-scope role change carries a course assignment dated from the transfer, and out-of-scope movers are removed from the denominator.

checklist.step: Track completion weekly and publish the gap
actions: Refresh the completion dashboard weekly from the LMS export: assigned, completed, passed, failed, overdue, by department and manager.
Show first-attempt pass rate separately from eventual completion — a low first-attempt rate signals content or comprehension problems.
Circulate the department league table to the Chief Claims Officer, the Head of Distribution and the Contact Center Ops Manager each Monday.
Flag any department below 80% complete at 15 November to the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: a weekly dashboard shows completion and first-attempt pass rate by department with a 15 November red-flag list issued.

checklist.step: Escalate non-completers through the agreed ladder
actions: At 1 December email every overdue learner and copy their line manager with the completion deadline extension of 15 days.
At day 45 send the remaining list to department heads with the Head of Compliance copied and request a written reason per person.
For anyone still outstanding, agree the compensating restriction with the department head — removal from claims authority or from customer-facing duty until completion.
Record every restriction, its start date and its lift date on the exception log.
checklist.done: every non-completer past day 45 has a written reason, a named compensating restriction and a dated exception log entry.

checklist.step: Analyse assessment answers for comprehension gaps and feed them back
actions: Export item-level assessment statistics and rank questions by failure rate.
Take the three worst questions and identify the Code obligation each tests.
Where failure exceeds 30%, either rewrite the module or raise a process issue — staff failing a question about claim denial reasons is a claims process signal, not only a training signal.
Send the analysis to the Chief Claims Officer and the Complaints Manager for process follow-up.
checklist.done: the three highest-failure questions are traced to their Code obligation with a rewrite or a process issue raised for each.

checklist.step: Report the completion outcome to the Compliance Committee and the board
actions: Prepare the December Compliance Committee paper: population, completion percentage, first-attempt pass rate, outstanding names by department, restrictions applied and comprehension findings.
State explicitly whether the annual obligation was met by 30 November, without softening language.
Upload the paper to the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting.
Record the committee's resolution and any directed action with an owner and a due date.
checklist.done: the committee paper states the completion outcome plainly and the minuted resolution carries owners and dates for any directed action.

checklist.step: Retain the training record set per the retention requirement
actions: Export from the LMS the per-employee completion register with assessment score, attempt count and completion timestamp.
Bundle it with the approved content version PDF, the mapping table, the attendance sheets and the exception log.
File under Insurance Code of Conduct / business conduct with the training year in the title and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the record can be retrieved by employee id and by department for an examiner request.
checklist.done: the year's training bundle is filed, labelled for 7 years, and retrievable by employee id and department.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum for the next cycle against the current Code text
actions: Re-read the BMA-published Code of Conduct for amendments since the last approval date and note every changed paragraph.
Fold the year's complaint root causes and the highest-failure assessment items into next year's scenarios.
Update the mapping table and re-approve the content version before 1 September.
Archive the prior content version rather than overwriting it, so past-year records still show what was taught.
checklist.done: next year's content version is mapped, approved before 1 September, and the prior version is archived intact.

testing.step: Build the in-scope population from the HRIS, not the LMS
actions: Extract all active workers at 30 November in the in-scope job families, plus all joiners, leavers and role changers during the year with effective dates.
Deliberately source the population from HRIS so an incomplete LMS learner group cannot shrink the denominator.
Record the report name, filters, run date and record count in the workpaper.
Have the extractor sign the extract as complete.
testing.done: a signed HRIS-sourced population exists with joiners, leavers and movers and their effective dates.

testing.step: Reconcile the LMS learner group to the HRIS population
actions: Export the LMS dynamic group membership and match it to the HRIS population on employee id.
List every HRIS in-scope worker with no LMS assignment — each is an automatic exception regardless of completion status elsewhere.
List every LMS assignment with no HRIS match and check for stale or duplicate accounts.
Quantify the difference and require a written explanation before sampling.
testing.done: the LMS group reconciles to the HRIS population with every unmatched worker on either side explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across departments and joiner types
actions: Take 100% of workers with claim settlement authority and 100% of licensed sales staff.
Take 40 further workers at random with a recorded seed, stratified across Claims, Distribution, Product, Complaints and Contact Centre.
Take 100% of joiners hired in the last quarter of the year, where the 30-day rule is most likely to be missed.
Record seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all settlement-authority and licensed staff, and includes every late-year joiner.

testing.step: Re-perform completion status and assessment scores in the LMS
actions: For each sampled worker open the transcript and read completion status, completion timestamp, attempt count and final score.
Confirm the score is at or above 80% and that an assessment attempt exists — a completion with zero attempts is a fail.
Confirm the completed course version matches the approved content version for the year.
Screenshot five transcripts into the workpaper as evidence of the read.
testing.done: every sampled transcript shows an assessment attempt, a score of at least 80% and the approved content version.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day joiner and role-change deadlines
actions: For each sampled joiner recompute due date = hire date + 30 calendar days and compare to the completion timestamp.
For each sampled role changer recompute due date = transfer effective date + 30 calendar days and compare.
For the annual population confirm completion on or before 30 November.
Tabulate days late per exception rather than recording only a yes/no.
testing.done: every sampled deadline is hand-recomputed with days-late quantified for each miss.

testing.step: Verify the curriculum genuinely covers the Code obligations it claims
actions: Take the mapping table and pick eight business-conduct obligations from the Bermuda Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) at random.
Open the module each row points at and confirm the obligation is actually taught, not merely referenced in a slide title.
Confirm the consequences-of-non-compliance paragraph is covered, including the BMA's ability to act on material failures.
Record a coverage verdict per obligation with the slide or screen reference.
testing.done: each of the eight sampled obligations is traced to specific taught content with a slide reference, or logged as a coverage gap.

testing.step: Test that untrained staff were actually restricted
actions: Take the day-45 non-completer list and pull each person's claim settlement authority and transaction history for the restriction period.
Confirm no claim decision or payment was made by a restricted user between the restriction start date and the completion date.
For sales staff, check the producer record for any new business written during the restriction window.
Any transaction inside a restriction window is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: no restricted user transacted during their restriction window, or each instance is raised as a breach.

testing.step: Trace the exception log and waiver approvals
actions: Match every day-45 non-completer to a GRC exception record with a written reason and a disposition.
Confirm each waiver or extension carries the Head of Compliance approval and pre-dates the extended due date.
Check that every exception has a closure date and that closure is supported by an LMS completion record.
List exceptions closed without a completion record as unsupported closures.
testing.done: every non-completer maps to an approved, dated exception and every closure is supported by an LMS completion record.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the employee id, the department, the days late and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause from the taxonomy: HRIS feed gap, manager non-escalation, leave of absence, contingent-worker onboarding gap, or refusal.
Set an owner at department-head level and a remediation date inside 30 days.
Carry unresolved exceptions into next year's assignment as mandatory day-one training.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a taxonomy root cause, a department-head owner, a 30-day remediation date and a carry-forward.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute completion percentage against the 100% threshold and the average first-attempt pass rate.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references for the population, sample and exceptions.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside Compliance and Learning & Development, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with completion percentage, pass rate, stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Capture every dissatisfaction expression from every channel into one register
actions: Open Cases ▸ New Complaint and record channel (phone, email, web form, broker, social, regulator letter), receipt date and time, policy number, product, and the complainant's own words verbatim.
Pull the originating contact from Genesys Cloud using the interaction id and attach the call recording or transcript to the case.
Check the Claims Platform and the billing record for the transaction the complaint refers to and link both to the case.
Set the acknowledgement SLA timer and the 30-day response timer at case creation, never later.
checklist.done: the case holds channel, receipt timestamp, verbatim complaint, linked transaction records and two running SLA timers.

checklist.step: Sweep the contact centre for dissatisfaction that never became a case
actions: Run the daily interaction report filtered to wrap-up codes 'Dissatisfied', 'Escalation requested' and 'Asked for a manager'.
Match each interaction to a complaint case id and list the unmatched ones.
Open a complaint case for every unmatched interaction that expresses dissatisfaction with a decision, a delay or a charge.
Send the daily unmatched count to the Complaints Manager — a persistent gap is a channel-capture failure, not a volume anomaly.
checklist.done: every dissatisfaction-coded interaction is matched to a case or has one opened, with a daily unmatched count reported.

checklist.step: Acknowledge the complainant within 5 business days
actions: Send the acknowledgement letter from the approved template naming the case reference, the handler, the expected response date and the escalation route if the complainant is dissatisfied with the outcome.
For regulator-forwarded complaints acknowledge to both the complainant and the forwarding regulator on the same day.
Record the acknowledgement despatch timestamp on the case — the timestamp, not a tick box, stops the SLA timer.
File the outbound letter to the case document tab.
checklist.done: an acknowledgement with the expected response date is despatched inside 5 business days and its timestamp is on the case.

checklist.step: Classify the complaint against the cause taxonomy and set severity
actions: Set the primary cause code from the taxonomy: claim decision, claim delay, sales suitability, disclosure clarity, premium or billing error, servicing error, data or privacy, or staff conduct.
Set severity using the agreed matrix — vulnerable customer, financial detriment above the delegated limit, litigation threat, media or regulator involvement all force High.
Assign the case to a handler outside the team that made the original decision, so the investigation is not marking its own work.
For High severity notify the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager the same day.
checklist.done: every case carries a taxonomy cause code, a matrix-derived severity and a handler independent of the original decision.

checklist.step: Investigate the case against the file and the applicable policy terms
actions: Read the full claim or policy file including adjuster notes, the coverage position and every letter sent to the policyholder.
Compare what was done to the policy wording, the published service standard and the fair-treatment expectations in the Code.
Where the decision turned on a technical exclusion, ask the Coverage Analyst for a written coverage view and attach it.
Write an investigation note stating whether the outcome was right, right but poorly explained, or wrong — with the reason for each.
Where wrong, quantify the detriment in currency and name the correcting action.
checklist.done: a written investigation note reaches a stated verdict with quantified detriment where the outcome was wrong.

checklist.step: Decide and deliver redress within the authority matrix
actions: Compute the redress: the correct claim amount, interest for the delay period, out-of-pocket costs evidenced by the complainant, and a distress and inconvenience element where the handling itself caused harm.
Check the amount against the authority matrix and route anything above the delegated limit to the Head of Compliance for approval before it is offered.
Raise the payment in the claims or billing system with the complaint case reference in the payment narrative so it can be traced later.
Record the offer date, the acceptance date and the payment clearing date on the case.
checklist.done: redress is computed, approved at the right level, paid with the case reference in the narrative, and the payment date is on the case.

checklist.step: Issue the substantive response inside 30 calendar days
actions: Write the final response covering what was complained about, what was found, what is being put right, and the redress amount with how it was calculated.
State the next-step escalation route and any applicable ombudsman or regulator contact details for the complainant's jurisdiction.
Where the 30 days cannot be met, send a holding letter before day 30 giving the reason and a new date, and log the reason as a delay exception.
Record the despatch timestamp and attach the letter to the case.
checklist.done: a substantive final response with findings, redress and escalation route is despatched inside 30 days, or a pre-day-30 holding letter is logged as an exception.

checklist.step: Answer regulator-forwarded complaints by the date on the regulator's letter
actions: Log every complaint arriving from the BMA or a US state department of insurance with the regulator's own reference and the response due date printed on the letter.
Prepare the response as a chronology with dated document exhibits rather than a narrative summary.
Have General Counsel review any response conceding an error before it leaves the building.
Submit through the regulator's stated channel and file the submission receipt against the case.
checklist.done: each regulator-forwarded complaint has a chronology response submitted by the regulator's stated date with a filed receipt.

checklist.step: Run the monthly root-cause forum on aggregated complaint data
actions: Refresh the complaints dashboard: volume by cause code, by product, by handling unit and by month, plus uphold rate and average days to close.
Rank the top five cause codes by volume and by total redress paid — they are not always the same list.
Chair the forum with Claims, Distribution, Billing and Product owners present and require a named owner for each of the top five.
Minute each agreed remediation with an owner, a due date and a measure of success stated as a target complaint volume.
checklist.done: the monthly forum minutes name an owner, a due date and a measurable target for each of the top five causes.

checklist.step: Set and monitor thresholds that trigger investigation automatically
actions: Define thresholds per cause code — for example a 50% month-on-month rise, more than 10 complaints on one product in a month, or any three complaints naming the same handler.
Configure dashboard alerts to email the Complaints Manager and the relevant process owner when a threshold trips.
Open a thematic review case within 5 business days of any trip and record the trigger data in it.
Review threshold levels quarterly so growth in the book does not mute the alerts.
checklist.done: thresholds are configured with automatic alerts, each trip opens a thematic review inside 5 business days, and levels are reviewed quarterly.

checklist.step: Drive remediation into the originating process and prove it landed
actions: Convert each forum action into a tracked remediation with the process owner named and the change described concretely — a letter rewrite, a system validation, a training module, a wording change.
For wording or letter changes, get the revised text approved by Compliance before release.
After the change lands, measure the complaint volume for that cause code over the following three months against the stated target.
Close the remediation only when the measured volume meets the target; otherwise reopen with a new action.
checklist.done: each remediation is closed only after three months of post-change complaint volume meets its stated target.

checklist.step: Identify affected non-complainants and extend redress where the cause was systemic
actions: Where a root cause is a systemic error, define the affected population by the same rule that caused it — product, date range, transaction type — not by who complained.
Ask the Data Analyst to extract the affected policy and claim list and reconcile the count to the system that produced the error.
Compute redress on the same basis as for the complainants and obtain Head of Compliance approval of the scheme.
Write to every affected policyholder and track acceptance and payment to completion.
checklist.done: every systemic cause has a defined affected population, an approved redress scheme and per-policyholder payment tracking.

checklist.step: Assess materiality and self-report failures to the BMA
actions: Apply the materiality criteria to each systemic finding: number of policyholders affected, aggregate detriment, duration undetected, and whether the failure touches the Code's business-conduct or integrity expectations.
Document the decision either way — a decision that a failure is not material must be written down with its reasoning, not left unrecorded.

Where material, prepare the self-report to the BMA setting out the failure, the population, the detriment, the remediation plan and the completion dates, and submit within 14 days of the materiality decision.
Notify the board and the Risk Committee on the same day the report is submitted, and file the submission receipt.
checklist.done: every systemic finding has a written materiality decision, and material failures are self-reported to the BMA within 14 days with the receipt filed.

checklist.step: Report complaint performance to the board committee
actions: Prepare the quarterly paper: volumes and trend, uphold rate, deadline adherence against the 5-day and 30-day standards, top causes, redress paid, open remediations and any BMA self-report.
Show adherence as a percentage against the 98% and 95% thresholds rather than as a narrative.
Upload to the board portal at least 5 business days before the committee meeting.
Minute the committee's direction and carry any directed action into the remediation tracker with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: the quarterly paper reports adherence against stated thresholds and every directed action is tracked with an owner and a date.

checklist.step: Retain the complaint files and feed the regulatory data submissions
actions: Archive each closed case with the original contact, all correspondence, the investigation note, the redress calculation and the closure letter.
Apply the 7-year-from-closure retention label and confirm retrieval by policy number, complainant name and cause code.
Supply the annual extract that feeds the NAIC MCAS complaint data elements to the Regulatory Reporting Manager by 15 March so the 30 April submission is not rushed.
Reconcile the extract count to the register count before hand-off and sign the reconciliation.
checklist.done: closed cases are archived under a 7-year label and a signed, reconciled MCAS extract is delivered by 15 March.

testing.step: Build the complaint population from every channel, not only the register
actions: Extract all complaint cases opened in the period with channel, receipt timestamp, acknowledgement timestamp, response timestamp, cause code, severity, redress amount and closure date.
Separately extract Genesys Cloud interactions with dissatisfaction wrap-up codes, the shared complaints mailbox item list, and the regulator correspondence log.
Union the sources so a complaint that never reached the register is still in the population.
Have the extractor sign the extract with queries, run date and counts.
testing.done: a signed union population covers case register, contact centre, mailbox and regulator correspondence for the period.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the source channels and quantify capture leakage
actions: Match dissatisfaction-coded interactions to case ids and count the unmatched.
Read 20 unmatched interaction transcripts and judge whether each expresses a complaint; every one that does is a capture exception.
Match every regulator letter in the correspondence log to a case and treat any unmatched letter as a critical exception.
Quantify the leakage rate and require a written explanation before sampling.
testing.done: capture leakage is quantified from read transcripts and every regulator letter is matched to a case or raised as critical.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of regulator-forwarded complaints and 100% of High-severity cases.
Take 40 further cases at random with a recorded seed, stratified across cause code and handling unit.
Take 10 cases closed as 'not upheld' with zero redress — the population where a wrong outcome is easiest to hide.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all regulator and High-severity cases plus a not-upheld stratum.

testing.step: Recompute the acknowledgement and response day counts
actions: Recompute acknowledgement days = despatch timestamp − receipt timestamp in business days, using the published holiday calendar.
Recompute response days = final response despatch − receipt in calendar days and compare to the 30-day standard.
For regulator-forwarded cases compare the submission date to the due date printed on the regulator's letter.
Check that any case exceeding 30 days has a holding letter despatched before day 30, and count days late where it does not.
testing.done: every sampled case has hand-recomputed day counts, days-late quantified, and holding letters verified against the 30-day point.

testing.step: Re-perform the classification and severity call independently
actions: Read the complainant's verbatim words and the investigation note without looking at the recorded cause code first.
Assign your own cause code and severity from the taxonomy and matrix, then compare.
Treat systematic downgrading — vulnerable customer or detriment cases coded Low — as a control failure rather than an individual error.
Confirm the handler was independent of the original decision on every sampled case.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent cause and severity call compared to the recorded one, with any downgrading pattern identified.

testing.step: Trace agreed redress to a cleared payment
actions: For every sampled case with agreed redress, search the payment records for the complaint case reference in the narrative.
Confirm the paid amount equals the approved amount and that interest was computed over the correct delay period.
Confirm payments above the delegated limit carry a pre-payment Head of Compliance approval.
List any agreed but unpaid redress as a zero-tolerance failure with the outstanding amount and the days elapsed.
testing.done: every agreed redress traces to a cleared payment of the approved amount, or the unpaid amount and days elapsed are listed.

testing.step: Test root-cause remediation actually closed and worked
actions: Take the last four monthly root-cause packs and list every action with its owner, due date and stated target.
Check the current status of each and quantify overdue days for those still open.
For actions marked closed, pull the three months of post-change complaint volume for that cause code and compare to the stated target.
Treat any action closed without the volume meeting its target as an unsupported closure.
testing.done: each remediation action is verified as open with days overdue, or closed with post-change volume meeting its stated target.

testing.step: Challenge the materiality decisions and BMA self-reporting
actions: List every systemic finding in the period and locate the written materiality decision for each.
Re-apply the materiality criteria yourself — affected population, aggregate detriment, duration undetected, Code obligation touched — and reach an independent conclusion.
For findings judged material, confirm the BMA self-report exists, recompute submission date against the 14-day window from the materiality decision, and read the filed receipt.
A systemic finding with no written materiality decision is a fail regardless of whether the outcome would have been non-material.
testing.done: every systemic finding has an independently re-performed materiality conclusion and material ones trace to a self-report inside 14 days.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the case reference, the deadline or amount missed and the policyholder impact.
Assign a root cause from the taxonomy: channel not captured, SLA timer not started, handler capacity, approval delay, wrong classification, or remediation not delivered.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with the Head of Compliance for any pattern suggesting a material failure.
Carry every open exception into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a taxonomy root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute acknowledgement and response adherence against the 98% and 95% thresholds and list every zero-tolerance breach separately.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references for population, leakage, sample and exceptions.
Have the reviewer, who handled no sampled case and approved no sampled redress, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with adherence percentages, listed zero-tolerance breaches, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Scope the audit and confirm it in the board-approved annual audit plan
actions: Open the annual audit plan entry for notice content and timing and list the notice types in scope by name.
State the third-line position explicitly — the audit is the independent assurance leg required by the Cyber Code's three-lines-of-defence expectation.
Confirm the auditors assigned hold no operational role in incident response, policy administration or compliance monitoring, and record the independence declarations.
Table the scope at the Audit Committee and record its approval and any committee-directed scope addition.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has approved a scope naming each notice type, with signed auditor independence declarations on file.

checklist.step: Build the notice rule table from the regulatory text, not from internal procedure
actions: For each notice type record: trigger event, statutory or Code deadline, the mandatory content elements, the required delivery method and the retention period.
For the BMA cyber notification record the 14-day window from the materiality assessment and the further 14-day follow-up window, citing the Cyber Code (2020).
Source each rule from the regulator's own published text and paste the sentence relied on into the row.
Send the table to the Compliance Officer for second-line confirmation that no rule is misstated before fieldwork opens.
checklist.done: each notice type has a rule row with trigger, deadline, content elements, delivery method and a quoted regulatory sentence, confirmed by second line.

checklist.step: Extract the notice population from the generating systems
actions: Extract from policy administration every notice generated in the period with notice type, policy number, trigger event date, generation date, despatch date and delivery method.
Extract from the ITSM record every BMA cyber notification with the materiality timestamp and the submission timestamp.
Add the print vendor's despatch file so notices generated but never mailed are visible.
Reconcile the three sources on counts by notice type and document every difference before proceeding.
checklist.done: a reconciled notice population exists across policy administration, ITSM and the print vendor despatch file, with differences documented.

checklist.step: Draw a statistical sample with a documented method
actions: Take 100% of BMA cyber notifications and 100% of non-renewal notices, where a timing miss has the largest consequence.
For each remaining notice type draw 25 items at random using a recorded seed, minimum 60 items in total.
Stratify by month so a systemic failure confined to one quarter cannot be missed.
Record seed, population size per type, sample size and selection date in the workpaper.
checklist.done: the sample is drawn per notice type with a recorded seed and monthly stratification, and covers all cyber and non-renewal notices.

checklist.step: Retrieve the actual notice images as sent
actions: For each sampled notice retrieve the archived image by policy number and generation date — the image, not the template.
Confirm the image is the version despatched, including any variable data merged into it.
List every sampled notice with no retrievable image as an evidence failure in its own right, since the company cannot prove what it sent.
Save each retrieved image into the audit file against the sample row.
checklist.done: every sampled notice has its as-sent image in the audit file, or is logged as an evidence failure.

checklist.step: Test notice content against the approved template and the rule table
actions: Compare each image line by line to the approved template version in force on the generation date.

Check every mandatory content element from the rule table is present: policy number, insured name and address, effective date of the action, the reason for the action, the statutory paragraph and the appeal or escalation route.
Check the merged variable data against the policy record — a correct template with the wrong effective date is still a fail.
Record a pass or fail per element per notice so the failure pattern is visible, not just a headline rate.
checklist.done: each sampled notice has an element-by-element content result tested against the template version in force on its generation date.

checklist.step: Test notice timing against the trigger event
actions: For each sampled notice recompute the deadline from the trigger event date and the rule table, using the correct calendar basis.
For BMA cyber notifications recompute submission due = materiality timestamp + 14 calendar days and the follow-up due = initial notification + 14 days.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the despatch or submission date and record days early or late.
Treat any late statutory notice as a finding immediately, without waiting for the sample to complete.
checklist.done: every sampled notice carries a hand-recomputed deadline and a days-early-or-late figure, with late statutory notices raised on the spot.

checklist.step: Test delivery and proof of despatch
actions: Match each sampled notice to the print vendor despatch confirmation and, where the rule requires it, the certificate of mailing or tracked delivery record.
For electronic delivery confirm a valid e-delivery consent exists on the policy record and pre-dates the notice.
Check returned-mail handling — an undelivered non-renewal notice with no re-issue is a substantive failure, not an administrative one.
Record the delivery evidence type and date against each sample row.
checklist.done: each sampled notice has despatch or delivery evidence of the type its rule requires, with returned mail traced to a re-issue.

checklist.step: Test that the three lines of defence actually operate on notices
actions: Confirm the first line runs a documented self-check on notice generation with dated evidence for the period.
Confirm the second line performs independent monitoring of notice timing and holds its own results, not a copy of the first line's.
Confirm no individual performs two of the three roles for the same notice type, using the entitlement export.
Where a line is absent or duplicated, raise it as a governance finding against the Cyber Code's 3LOD expectation.
checklist.done: first-line self-check and second-line monitoring evidence exist separately for the period, with role duplication tested and any gap raised as a governance finding.

checklist.step: Interview the process owners on the failures found
actions: Walk the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Incident Response Lead through the specific failed items rather than summary statistics.
Establish for each whether the cause is template configuration, trigger data quality, batch scheduling, vendor handover or human judgement.
Confirm whether the failure was already known to the first or second line — a known, untreated failure is a more serious finding.
Minute each interview with attendees, date and the agreed factual position.
checklist.done: each failure category has a minuted, owner-agreed root cause and a stated position on whether it was already known.

checklist.step: Document the workpapers so the test can be re-performed by a stranger
actions: Index the file: scope, rule table, population extracts and reconciliations, sampling record with seed, per-item test sheets, retrieved images, interview minutes.
Cross-reference every assertion in the draft report to a workpaper reference.
Have the audit lead perform a review sign-off on each workpaper with review notes cleared and dated.
Lock the workpapers to read-only at fieldwork close on 30 September.
checklist.done: the file is indexed, every report assertion is cross-referenced, review notes are cleared and workpapers are locked at fieldwork close.

checklist.step: Rate the findings and agree management actions
actions: Rate each finding Significant, Moderate or Low against the agreed criteria — any missed BMA 14-day notification is Significant by definition.
Agree a specific management action with each owner: a template change, a validation rule, a batch schedule change, not a promise to be careful.
Set due dates proportionate to the rating — Significant within 60 days, Moderate within 120 days.
Obtain the written management response from each owner within 10 business days of the draft report.
checklist.done: every finding carries a rating, a specific owner-agreed action, a rating-proportionate due date and a written management response.

checklist.step: Issue the report to the Audit Committee
actions: Issue the final report with the scope, the population and sample sizes, the content and timing results as measured rates, the findings and the overall opinion.
State the opinion in plain terms — satisfactory, needs improvement or unsatisfactory — and say what it means for the Cyber Code's independent assurance expectation.
Upload to the board portal at least 5 business days before the Q4 Audit Committee and present in person.
Minute the committee's acceptance and any directed additional work.
checklist.done: the final report with a stated opinion is tabled at the Q4 Audit Committee and its acceptance is minuted.

checklist.step: Track findings to validated closure
actions: Track each action in the findings tracker with owner, due date and current status, refreshed monthly.
On the claimed completion date obtain the evidence — the changed template version, the validation rule screenshot, the corrected notice sample — and re-test a small sample.
Close the finding only on inspected evidence; record management's assertion separately from your validation.
Escalate any Significant finding overdue by 30 days to the Audit Committee chair.
checklist.done: each finding is closed only on inspected, re-tested evidence, and Significant findings overdue by 30 days reach the committee chair.

checklist.step: Retain the audit file for the retention period
actions: Copy the signed report, the workpaper index and the findings tracker export into the compliance evidence repository under Cyber Code / independent assurance.
Apply the 7-year-from-issue retention label to the audit file and its workpapers.
Confirm retrieval by audit year, notice type and finding rating for a future BMA request.
Record the archive completion date on the audit record.
checklist.done: the audit file is archived under a 7-year label and retrievable by year, notice type and finding rating.

testing.step: Rebuild the audit's own population independently
actions: Re-extract notices for the audit period using your own query rather than the audit's saved extract.
Compare counts by notice type to the audit's population and investigate every difference above 1%.
Confirm the audit population included the print vendor despatch file and the ITSM cyber notification records.
Sign the re-extract with query, run date and counts.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt population is reconciled to the audit's population with every difference above 1% investigated.

testing.step: Reconcile the audit population to the source of record
actions: Compare the notice population to the count of archived notice images for the same period and dates.
List notice types present in the document repository but absent from the audit scope — an out-of-scope notice type with a statutory deadline is a scope gap.
Confirm the cyber notification count matches the incident register's count of material incidents.
Document each reconciling item with its explanation.
testing.done: the audit population reconciles to the document repository and incident register, with any scope gap named.

testing.step: Re-draw the sample and confirm the audit's selection was unbiased
actions: Re-run the sampling using the recorded seed and confirm it reproduces the audit's sample exactly.
Check the sample covers every month and every notice type in the scope, and that the 100% strata were genuinely complete.
Draw 15 additional items outside the audit's sample for independent re-testing.
Record the re-draw method, seed and selection date.
testing.done: the audit's sample is reproduced from its seed, the strata are confirmed complete, and 15 fresh items are selected.

testing.step: Re-perform the content test on the fresh items
actions: Retrieve the as-sent image for each of the 15 fresh items and the approved template version in force on the generation date.
Test the mandatory content elements from the regulatory text yourself before reading the audit's rule table, then compare the two.
Flag any element the audit's rule table omits — a wrong rule table produces a clean audit over a non-compliant process.
Record a pass or fail per element with the image reference.
testing.done: 15 fresh items are content-tested against the regulatory text independently, and every omission in the audit's rule table is flagged.

testing.step: Recompute the timing maths including the BMA 14-day windows
actions: Recompute the deadline for each fresh item from its trigger event date and the regulatory rule, on the correct calendar basis.
For every material cyber incident recompute notification due = materiality timestamp + 14 calendar days and follow-up due = initial notification + 14 days.
Compare each recomputation to the audit's recorded result and to the actual despatch or submission date.
Quantify days late per item rather than recording a pass or fail alone.
testing.done: every fresh item and every cyber notification has an independently recomputed deadline with days-late quantified.

testing.step: Trace the audit's assertions to workpaper evidence
actions: Pick ten assertions from the audit report and follow each cross-reference into the workpaper.
Confirm the workpaper actually supports the assertion, including the retrieved images and the interview minutes.
Confirm review notes were cleared and the workpapers were locked at fieldwork close.
List any assertion with no supporting workpaper as an unsupported conclusion.
testing.done: each of the ten sampled report assertions is traced to supporting, reviewed and locked workpaper evidence.

testing.step: Test auditor independence and 3LOD separation
actions: Read the signed independence declarations for every auditor on the engagement.
Export the auditors' system entitlements and confirm none holds write access to policy administration notice configuration or the ITSM incident record type.
Confirm no auditor performed first- or second-line notice monitoring during the audit period.
Any breach of independence invalidates the assurance and is reported directly to the Audit Committee chair.
testing.done: every auditor's independence is confirmed by declaration and entitlement export, with any breach escalated to the committee chair.

testing.step: Verify findings were tracked, validated and not closed on assertion
actions: List every finding from the prior and current audit with rating, owner, due date and status.
For each closed finding, inspect the closure evidence and confirm a re-test was performed rather than a management assertion accepted.
Recompute days overdue for open findings and check that Significant findings past 30 days reached the Audit Committee chair.
List closures without re-test evidence as unsupported.
testing.done: every closed finding shows inspected re-test evidence and every overdue Significant finding shows a documented escalation.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception — scope gap, rule table error, unsupported assertion, independence breach or unsupported closure.
Assign a root cause and an owner within Internal Audit or the operating team as appropriate.
Set a remediation date and, where a real notice was late, open a separate operational breach issue with the notice owner.
Carry every open exception into the next audit cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a carry-forward into the next cycle.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the re-performance agreement rate between the audit's results and the independent re-test, and list every zero-tolerance timing breach separately.
Write the conclusion on whether the third-line assurance over notices can be relied on, citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither generated notices nor performed the audit fieldwork, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an agreement rate, listed timing breaches, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.
