checklist.step: Maintain the charter register for the board and every committee
actions: Hold one register row per body — board, Audit, Risk, Nomination and Governance, Investment, Remuneration — with charter version, approval date, next review date and approving resolution reference.
Store the current charter PDF against each row and archive superseded versions rather than overwriting them.
Check every charter states purpose, membership and independence requirements, quorum, meeting frequency, delegated authority and reporting line to the board.
Flag any body operating without an approved current charter to the General Counsel the same week.
checklist.done: every board body has a current approved charter in the register with version, approval date and next review date, and archived predecessors.

checklist.step: Review each charter annually against the Code's governance requirements
actions: Read s.5 (Corporate Governance) and s.6 (compliance function, internal audit function) of the Bermuda Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) and list each board-level requirement.
Map each requirement to the charter clause that satisfies it, quoting the clause text on the mapping row.
Where no clause satisfies a requirement, draft the clause and route it through the Nomination and Governance Committee for board approval.
Present the mapping and any drafted clauses to the committee at its first meeting of the year.
checklist.done: every Code governance requirement maps to a quoted charter clause, and any unmapped requirement has a drafted clause before the committee.

checklist.step: Test committee composition, independence and quorum against the charters
actions: Build the composition schedule: for each body list members, appointment date, executive or non-executive status, independence status and any chair role held elsewhere.
Compare the actual composition to the charter requirement — for example an Audit Committee majority of independent non-executives and an independent chair who is not the board chair.
Check no individual sits in a combination the Code discourages, such as chairing both Audit and Risk without a documented rationale.
Escalate any shortfall to the Nomination and Governance Committee with a proposed appointment timetable.
checklist.done: a composition schedule shows each body against its charter requirement, with every shortfall escalated with a proposed appointment date.

checklist.step: Maintain the board skills and experience matrix
actions: List the competency axes the business needs on the board: insurance underwriting, actuarial, investments, cyber and technology risk, regulatory and legal, audit and finance.
Score each director's depth on each axis from their biography and their declared experience, and have each director confirm their own row.
Identify the thinnest axis — a board with no member able to challenge a cyber risk report cannot discharge the Cyber Code's governance expectation.
Feed the gaps into the Nomination and Governance Committee's succession plan with target recruitment dates.
checklist.done: a director-confirmed skills matrix identifies the thinnest competency axes and they are carried into the succession plan with dates.

checklist.step: Fix the annual meeting calendar and check it meets charter minimums
actions: Publish the following year's calendar each December with board and committee dates, paper deadlines and distribution dates.
Count scheduled meetings per body against the charter minimum — Audit and Risk typically at least four a year — and add dates where short.
Sequence committee meetings ahead of the board meeting they report into, so committee minutes are available to the board.
Circulate for director availability and lock the dates before the year starts.
checklist.done: next year's calendar is published in December, meets or exceeds every charter minimum, and sequences committees ahead of the board.

checklist.step: Plan each agenda from the charter's duty list, not from last meeting's agenda
actions: Build an annual agenda plan mapping every charter duty to the meeting at which it will be discharged.
Cover the mandatory recurring items: compliance function report, internal audit report, risk appetite review, cyber risk report, capital and solvency, and complaints and conduct.
Draft each agenda from the plan and mark items 'for decision', 'for discussion' or 'for noting' so decision items are unmistakable.
Reconcile at year end that every charter duty was in fact covered and list any that were not.
checklist.done: an annual agenda plan maps every charter duty to a meeting, and the year-end reconciliation names any duty not covered.

checklist.step: Guarantee the compliance function's direct quarterly reporting line
actions: Table a compliance report at least quarterly covering the monitoring plan status, breaches and self-reports, complaint conduct metrics and regulatory change.
Include a standing statement of whether the compliance function had unrestricted access to information and adequate resources in the quarter.
Hold a private session with the committee without executive management present at least twice a year and have it minuted as held.
Escalate immediately, outside the calendar, any material failure to comply with the Code or the Act rather than waiting for the next quarterly slot.
checklist.done: four compliance reports a year are minuted, two private sessions are recorded, and material failures are escalated between meetings.

checklist.step: Guarantee the internal audit function's reporting line and unrestricted access
actions: Confirm the internal audit charter states a functional reporting line to the Audit Committee chair and an administrative line only to management.
Table the annual audit plan for Audit Committee approval and report plan completion at each meeting.
Record any management restriction on scope, access or resources in the committee paper the quarter it occurs.
Hold a private session with the Audit Committee at least twice a year and have it minuted.
checklist.done: the audit charter shows a functional line to the committee chair, the plan is approved and tracked, and private sessions are minuted.

checklist.step: Produce and distribute board packs at least 5 business days ahead
actions: Collect papers against the paper deadline set in the calendar and chase owners at T-15 and T-12 business days.
Assemble the pack with agenda, prior minutes, action tracker, and each paper carrying an author, a purpose and a recommendation.
Publish to the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting and record the publication timestamp.
Log any paper tabled after distribution as a late paper with the reason and the author, and report the count to the chair.
checklist.done: the pack is published with a recorded timestamp at least 5 business days ahead, and every late paper is logged with author and reason.

checklist.step: Record attendance and test quorum before business is transacted
actions: Record attendance at the start of the meeting including those joining remotely, apologies and any late arrivals with times.
Compare attendance to the charter quorum, including any requirement for an independent member or a specific role to be present.
Where quorum is not met, record that no decisions were taken and reconvene rather than proceeding.
Note the point at which any member leaves, so decisions taken after their departure can be quorum-tested separately.
checklist.done: attendance with timings is recorded, quorum is tested against the charter before decisions, and inquorate meetings take no decisions.

checklist.step: Take minutes to the agreed standard and approve them at the next meeting
actions: Minute for each item the papers received, the substance of the challenge and debate, the decision taken, and any dissent recorded by name.
Record the reasoning behind decisions on risk, capital and conduct matters — a minute reading only 'the report was noted' cannot evidence board oversight to the BMA.
Circulate the draft within 10 business days for comment and table it for approval at the next meeting.
File the approved and signed minutes in the legal document system and mark the portal copy as approved.
checklist.done: minutes record papers, challenge, decision and dissent, are circulated within 10 business days and approved at the next meeting.

checklist.step: Track board and committee actions to closure
actions: Open an action tracker row for every action with the owner, the required outcome, the due date and the meeting that raised it.
Refresh status before each meeting and present the tracker as a standing agenda item with overdue items listed by owner.
Require evidence of completion, not an owner's verbal confirmation, before an action is marked closed.
Escalate any action overdue by two meetings to the committee chair in writing.
checklist.done: every action has an owner, a due date and evidence-based closure, with two-meeting overdue items escalated to the chair in writing.

checklist.step: Capture conflicts of interest declared at every meeting
actions: Open each meeting with the standing conflicts item and record any declaration against the specific agenda item it affects.
Where a conflict is declared, minute whether the member withdrew, abstained or participated with permission, and re-test quorum for that item.
Update the standing conflicts register with the declaration, the date and the treatment applied.
Reconcile meeting declarations to the annual declaration forms and query any conflict declared in one but not the other.
checklist.done: each declared conflict is minuted against its agenda item with the treatment applied, and the register reconciles to the annual forms.

checklist.step: Run the annual board and committee effectiveness review
actions: Issue the evaluation questionnaire covering composition, information quality, pack timeliness, quality of challenge, committee interaction and chair effectiveness.
Collect responses confidentially and analyse them by body rather than reporting a single aggregate score.
Present findings to the Nomination and Governance Committee with a specific improvement action per weak area, each with an owner and a date.
Record the review's completion and its actions in the board minutes so the BMA can see it was performed.
checklist.done: the annual evaluation is completed per body with owner-and-date improvement actions minuted at board level.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA of board and officer changes and retain the record set
actions: On every appointment or resignation of a director, controller or officer, prepare the BMA notification with the effective date and the fitness assessment reference.
Submit within the Insurance Act notification window and file the submission receipt against the appointment record.
Update the composition schedule, the board portal membership and the statutory registers the same week.
Archive charters, minutes, packs and attendance registers under a 10-year retention label and confirm retrieval by body, meeting date and resolution reference.
checklist.done: every officer change is notified with a filed receipt and registers updated the same week, with records archived under a 10-year label.

testing.step: Build the population of meetings, members and actions for the period
actions: Extract every board and committee meeting in the period with date, body, attendees, apologies and minute approval status.
Extract the membership history with appointment and resignation effective dates, and the full action tracker.
Add the current charter set with version and approval dates.
Have the extractor sign the extract with the queries, run date and record counts.
testing.done: a signed population covers meetings, attendance, membership history, actions and the charter set for the period.

testing.step: Reconcile the meeting register to the charter-mandated minimums and the calendar
actions: Count meetings actually held per body and compare to the charter minimum and to the published annual calendar.
List every calendared meeting that was cancelled or postponed and the reason recorded.
Reconcile the minute set to the meeting register — a meeting held with no minutes is a critical exception.
Document every difference before sampling.
testing.done: meetings held reconcile to the charter minimum, the calendar and the minute set, with every cancellation and gap explained.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample of meetings
actions: Take 100% of Audit and Risk Committee meetings and 100% of meetings that approved a policy, an appointment or a capital action.
Take 8 further meetings at random with a recorded seed across the remaining bodies.
Take 100% of appointments and resignations in the period.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all Audit and Risk meetings, all decision meetings and all membership changes, and is reproducible from the seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the quorum and composition test on each sampled meeting
actions: Read the charter quorum and composition clause in force on the meeting date, not the current version.
Count the attendees present at the time each decision was taken, allowing for members who arrived late or left early.
Confirm any required independent member or role-holder was present for the decisions requiring them.
Any decision taken without quorum or required composition is a fail reported immediately to General Counsel.
testing.done: each sampled decision is quorum- and composition-tested against the charter version in force, with failures reported immediately.

testing.step: Trace agenda coverage back to charter duties
actions: Take each charter duty for the Audit and Risk Committees and search the year's agendas and minutes for the meeting that discharged it.
Confirm the minute shows substantive treatment, not a title on an agenda with no recorded discussion.
List every duty with no evidenced discharge in the year.
Cross-check the year-end reconciliation the secretariat performed and note anything it missed.
testing.done: each charter duty is traced to a minuted, substantive discussion, or listed as undischarged with the secretariat's reconciliation checked.

testing.step: Verify the compliance and internal audit reporting lines operated
actions: Count compliance function reports tabled at board or committee level in the year and confirm at least one per quarter with no quarter missed.
Confirm two minuted private sessions each for compliance and internal audit without executive management present.
Read the reports for any recorded restriction on access, resources or scope and check what the board did about it.
A quarter with no compliance report is a fail against s.5/s.6 regardless of the annual total.
testing.done: each quarter shows a tabled compliance report, private sessions are minuted for both functions, and every recorded restriction has a board response.

testing.step: Recompute pack distribution lead times and minute approval timing
actions: For each sampled meeting recompute lead days = publication timestamp to meeting date in business days and compare to the 5-business-day standard.
Count late-tabled papers per meeting and identify the repeat offending authors.
Recompute days from meeting to draft minute circulation against the 10-business-day standard and confirm approval at the next meeting.
Compute the adherence rate against the 95% distribution and 100% approval thresholds.
testing.done: lead times and minute approval timings are hand-recomputed with adherence rates against the stated thresholds.

testing.step: Test action closure and conflicts capture
actions: Age every open action from its due date and identify those overdue by two or more meetings without a written chair escalation.
For 15 closed actions inspect the closure evidence and confirm it demonstrates the required outcome rather than asserting completion.
Reconcile conflicts declared in meeting minutes to the standing conflicts register and to the annual declaration forms.
Confirm each declared conflict shows a minuted treatment and, where withdrawal occurred, a re-tested quorum for that item.
testing.done: action ageing and escalations are verified, 15 closures are evidence-inspected, and conflicts reconcile across minutes, register and annual forms.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the body, the meeting date and the governance requirement missed.
Assign a root cause: charter not updated, appointment not made, secretariat capacity, paper author delay, or minute quality.
Set an owner — the committee chair for composition and quorum failures, the Corporate Secretary for process failures — and a remediation date.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, a named chair or secretariat owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State adherence against each threshold — quorum and composition zero tolerance, 95% pack distribution, 100% minute approval, quarterly compliance reporting.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references behind each element.
Have the reviewer, who is independent of the secretariat and minuted no sampled meeting, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Nomination and Governance Committee and the Audit Committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with per-threshold adherence, a stated conclusion and committee reporting dates exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Maintain the governance filing calendar against the statutes that create the filings
actions: Hold one calendar row per filing: filing name, legal entity, regulator, statutory basis, due date rule, preparer, reviewer, certifier and submission channel.
Set the CGAD row to 1 June annually, the Form B row to 120 days after fiscal year end, and the Form F row to the same cycle.
Add the event-driven rows — Form A change of control, Form D 30-day prior notice, BMA officer and controller notifications — as trigger rows with no fixed date.
Review the calendar against the current statute list each January and record the review date on each row.
checklist.done: every governance filing has a calendar row citing its statutory basis, due-date rule and named preparer, reviewer and certifier, reviewed each January.

checklist.step: Confirm the lead state and the reporting group structure before drafting
actions: Confirm the lead state designation for the insurance holding company system and whether it changed since last year's filing.
List every insurer in the group, its domiciliary state or Bermuda registration, and whether the CGAD is filed at the ultimate controlling person or the insurer level.
Confirm which Bermuda entities fall under the Insurance Code of Conduct and the Cyber Code so the cyber governance content is scoped correctly.
Record the conclusion with the date and the source, and notify the Corporate Secretary of any change in filing level.
checklist.done: the lead state, the filing level and the Bermuda entity scope are confirmed in writing with a source and a date before drafting begins.

checklist.step: Collect the governance content from the committee and function owners
actions: Issue a content request in March to the Corporate Secretary, Head of Compliance, Chief Audit Executive, Chief Risk Officer and Chief HR Officer with a two-week return date.

Request for each: board and committee structure and composition, director qualification and independence process, board evaluation process, succession planning, remuneration policy, and the risk, compliance, internal audit and actuarial function descriptions.
For the cyber governance content request the three-lines-of-defence description showing operational management, risk management and independent assurance roles, as the Cyber Code expects.
Reconcile every submitted description to the charters and minutes rather than accepting it at face value.
checklist.done: every CGAD content section has an owner-submitted description reconciled to the charters and minutes, returned by the March deadline.

checklist.step: Draft the disclosure and mark what changed since last year
actions: Draft against the lead state's CGAD content requirements section by section, so the filing follows the regulator's structure and not the company's.
Produce a redline against the prior year's filed version and list every substantive change with the board decision or minute that caused it.
Where a practice described last year has stopped, say so plainly rather than deleting the sentence silently.
Circulate the draft with the redline to the content owners for factual confirmation.
checklist.done: a draft following the regulator's required structure exists with a prior-year redline, each change traced to a board decision and confirmed by its owner.

checklist.step: Obtain legal review and clear the confidentiality position
actions: Review the draft for statements that overstate a practice — a described control that does not operate is a misstatement to the regulator, not a presentational issue.
Confirm the confidential treatment the CGAD statute affords and prepare the confidentiality request or legend the lead state requires.
Check the disclosure is consistent with the Form F enterprise risk report, the Financial Condition Report and any public filings for the same period.
Record legal clearance with the version number and the clearance date.
checklist.done: legal clearance is recorded against a version number, with the confidentiality position set and cross-filing consistency checked.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer certification signature
actions: Provide the certifying officer with the final draft, the content owner confirmations and the prior-year redline before signature is requested.
Have the officer sign the certification that the disclosure is accurate and that the described governance framework is in place.
Capture the signature through the e-signature platform with an audit certificate showing signer identity and timestamp.
Where the officer will not certify a section, stop the filing and fix the underlying practice rather than softening the wording.
checklist.done: a timestamped officer certification is captured with an audit certificate, on the same version that will be filed.

checklist.step: Submit the CGAD to the lead state by 1 June
actions: Assemble the submission package: signed disclosure, certification, confidentiality request and any exhibits the lead state's instructions demand.
Submit through the lead state's stated channel on or before 1 June and record the submission timestamp.
Capture the acknowledgement or receipt and file it against the calendar row — a submission with no captured receipt is treated as unfiled.
Update the calendar row to 'Filed' with the submission date, the receipt reference and the filed version number.
checklist.done: the CGAD is submitted by 1 June with a captured receipt and the calendar row updated with date, receipt and version.

checklist.step: Prepare and file the holding company Form B and Form F
actions: Build the Form B registration statement with the current organisational chart, the ultimate controlling person, and every affiliate agreement and intercompany transaction in force.
Reconcile the affiliate agreement list to the contract system and the general ledger intercompany balances, and explain any difference in the filing.
Prepare the Form F enterprise risk report covering material developments in the group's risk profile, and keep it consistent with the CGAD's risk function description.
File within 120 days of fiscal year end and capture the receipt against the calendar row.
checklist.done: Form B and Form F are filed within 120 days of fiscal year end, reconciled to the contract system and ledger, with receipts captured.

checklist.step: Monitor for event-driven filing triggers continuously
actions: Run a monthly sweep of board minutes, HRIS officer records, the share register and the contract system for events that create a filing obligation.

Flag for Form D any proposed affiliate transaction — management agreement, reinsurance pooling, cost sharing, guarantee — and start the 30-day prior notice clock from the intended effective date working backwards.
Flag for Form A any acquisition of 10% or more of voting securities and escalate to General Counsel the day it is identified.
Log each detected trigger with the detection date and the computed filing deadline.
checklist.done: a monthly sweep across minutes, HRIS, share register and contracts logs each trigger with a detection date and a computed deadline.

checklist.step: File the Form D prior notice at least 30 days before the transaction
actions: Compute the submission date as the intended effective date minus 30 days minus an internal preparation buffer of 10 business days.
Prepare the notice with the transaction terms, the fairness rationale and the effect on the insurer's surplus, supported by the Chief Financial Officer's figures.
Submit to the domiciliary regulator and hold the transaction until the notice period expires without disapproval.
Record the non-disapproval date and release the transaction to the contract owner in writing.
checklist.done: each affiliate transaction has a Form D filed at least 30 days ahead and is not executed before the notice period expires.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA of controller and officer changes within the statutory window
actions: On each appointment or departure of a director, officer or controller of a Bermuda entity, prepare the notification with the effective date and the fitness assessment reference.
Compute the notification deadline from the effective date under the Insurance Act window and load it into the calendar as a dated row.
Submit through the BMA's electronic filing channel and capture the receipt.
Where the change affects the cyber governance roles described under the Cyber Code, notify within 14 days of the change taking effect.
checklist.done: every Bermuda officer or controller change has a submitted notification inside its statutory window with a captured receipt.

checklist.step: Track regulator acknowledgements and answer follow-up questions
actions: Open a tracker item for every filing awaiting acknowledgement and chase anything unacknowledged after 15 business days.
Log each regulator question with the date received and a target response inside 14 days unless the regulator states a shorter date.
Draft responses with the supporting exhibit attached rather than a narrative assurance, and have General Counsel clear anything conceding a deficiency.
Close the tracker item only on the regulator's confirmation, and file the full exchange with the filing.
checklist.done: every filing has a tracked acknowledgement and every regulator question is answered within 14 days with exhibits and a filed exchange.

checklist.step: Report the filing status to the board
actions: Table a filing status paper at the committee meeting following each filing cycle listing filings due, filed, late and outstanding with dates.
Confirm to the board that the certifying officer's statements were supported by the charters, minutes and function descriptions.
Report any regulator question and its answer, and any voluntary disclosure made.
Minute the board's noting and any directed action with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: a filing status paper with filed, late and outstanding items is minuted at the committee following each cycle.

checklist.step: Run a year-end look-back for filings that should have been made
actions: Compare the year's events — officer changes, affiliate transactions, ownership movements, structural changes — to the filings actually made.
For each event with no filing, determine whether an obligation existed and document the reasoning either way.
Where an obligation was missed, prepare a late filing with a covering explanation and take General Counsel's decision on voluntary disclosure.
Feed each miss into the trigger-detection sweep so the same event type is caught next year.
checklist.done: every event in the year is matched to a filing or a written no-obligation conclusion, with misses filed late and disclosed on counsel's decision.

checklist.step: Retain the filing record set under confidential treatment
actions: Archive each filing with its content workpapers, legal markup, signed certification, submission receipt and regulator correspondence.
Apply the 7-year-from-filing retention label and the confidentiality marking the statute grants to CGAD material.
Restrict access to the secretariat, legal and compliance groups and record the access list.
Confirm retrieval by filing name, legal entity, regulator and filing year.
checklist.done: each filing is archived with its full support under a 7-year confidential label, access-restricted and retrievable by entity and year.

testing.step: Build the population of filings required and filings made
actions: Extract the filing calendar rows for the year with statutory basis, due date, status, submission date and receipt reference.
Extract separately every submission receipt held for the year, so a filing made outside the calendar is still visible.
Extract the event sources — board minutes, HRIS officer changes, share register movements and affiliate contracts executed.
Have the extractor sign each extract with query, run date and counts.
testing.done: signed extracts cover calendar rows, held receipts and the underlying event sources for the year.

testing.step: Reconcile the calendar to the statutes rather than to itself
actions: Build an independent list of governance filings the group owes from the lead state's CGAD adoption, the holding company act forms and the Bermuda Insurance Act notification requirements.
Match the independent list to the calendar rows and list every obligation with no calendar row — a missing row is how a filing is missed silently.
Confirm the due-date rule on each row matches the statute, including the 1 June CGAD date and the 120-day Form B rule.
Document every difference with the statutory reference before sampling.
testing.done: an independently built statutory filing list reconciles to the calendar, with every missing row and wrong due-date rule documented.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of filings and events
actions: Take 100% of annual filings — CGAD, Form B, Form F — and 100% of Form A and Form D notices.
Take 100% of Bermuda officer and controller changes in the year.
Take 15 further event-driven items at random with a recorded seed from the monthly sweep logs.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers every annual filing, every Form A/D and officer change, plus 15 seeded event items.

testing.step: Recompute every filing deadline from its statutory rule
actions: Recompute the CGAD deadline as 1 June and the Form B deadline as fiscal year end plus 120 days for the filing entity.
Recompute each Form D deadline as the transaction effective date minus 30 days and compare to the actual submission date.
Recompute each BMA officer notification deadline from the effective date under the Insurance Act window.
Record days early or late per filing rather than a pass or fail alone.
testing.done: every sampled filing has a hand-recomputed statutory deadline with days early or late quantified.

testing.step: Trace each filing to a regulator receipt and the filed version
actions: Open the archived submission package for each sampled filing and read the receipt or acknowledgement reference and date.
Confirm the archived version is the version certified — compare the document hash or version number on the certification to the filed document.
Confirm the confidentiality request or legend was included where the statute grants it.
Treat any filing with no captured receipt as unfiled for testing purposes.
testing.done: each sampled filing traces to a captured receipt and the archived version matches the certified version.

testing.step: Verify the officer certification is genuine, dated and pre-submission
actions: Open the e-signature audit certificate for each certification and read signer identity, email, IP and timestamp.
Confirm the signature timestamp pre-dates the submission timestamp — a certification signed after filing is a fail.
Confirm the certifying officer holds the office the statute names.
Capture the audit certificate into the workpaper.
testing.done: each certification has an audit certificate showing the correct officer signing before submission, captured in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the CGAD content against the charters and minutes
actions: Take eight assertions from the filed CGAD — committee composition, board evaluation, independence process, three-lines-of-defence cyber roles, compliance function reporting.
Verify each against the charters, the minutes and the function descriptions in force during the disclosure year.
Flag any assertion describing a practice that did not actually operate — an overstated control in a certified filing is a misstatement to the regulator.
Record a verdict and the supporting minute reference per assertion.
testing.done: eight CGAD assertions are independently verified to charters and minutes, with any overstated practice flagged as a misstatement.

testing.step: Reconcile the year's events to the filings they should have produced
actions: List every officer and director appointment and departure from HRIS and the board minutes with effective dates.
List every affiliate agreement executed from the contract system and every ownership movement from the share register.
Match each event to a filing or to a documented no-obligation conclusion, and list the unmatched.
For any event whose deadline has already passed with no filing, escalate to General Counsel the same day.
testing.done: every officer change, affiliate agreement and ownership movement is matched to a filing or a written no-obligation conclusion.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the filing, the entity, the statutory deadline and the days late or the content deficiency.
Assign a root cause: calendar row missing, trigger not detected, content owner late, certification delay, or receipt not captured.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and record General Counsel's decision on voluntary disclosure for every late or missed filing.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly trigger test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a recorded voluntary-disclosure decision where filing was late.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the result against the zero-tolerance threshold: filings made, filings late with days late, filings missed, certifications missing and receipts missing.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references behind each element.
Have the reviewer, who drafted, reviewed and submitted none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper listing late and missed filings, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: General Counsel owns the fitness and propriety standard and the conflicts policy; HR Business Partner runs the screening pack for each appointment and the Corporate Secretary holds the conflicts register and the BMA notification

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Bermuda Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) s.5 (Corporate Governance), including the conflicts of interest requirements for directors, officers and related parties, read with the Insurance Act fitness and propriety expectations for controllers and officers; re-read at each policy review

In-scope processes.value: Appointment and re-appointment of directors, officers, controllers and holders of key functions — compliance, internal audit, risk, actuarial — from nomination through screening, conflicts declaration, board approval, regulator notification and annual re-attestation

In-scope systems.value: Appointment records and annual attestation campaigns in the HRIS, screening results from the background and sanctions vendors, declarations executed by e-signature, and the conflicts register held in the board portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: Fitness and Propriety and Conflicts of Interest Procedure — in-scope position list, screening pack contents, adverse-finding escalation, conflicts declaration and register maintenance, board approval, regulator notification and annual re-attestation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the board on the Nomination and Governance Committee's recommendation; reviewed annually and after any adverse finding that the procedure failed to surface before appointment

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per appointment — the complete screening pack must be signed off before the appointment effective date, never after; the BMA notification of a new or departing officer or controller is due inside the Insurance Act window measured from the effective date; annual re-attestation of continuing fitness and conflicts is due by 31 January each year

Deadline reminders configured.value: HRIS task reminders to the HR Business Partner at 10 and 5 business days before a scheduled appointment effective date where the pack is incomplete, a Corporate Secretary alert on the day an effective date is recorded so the notification clock starts, and attestation campaign reminders on 5, 15 and 25 January

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Screening pack, search results with run dates, references, declarations, competence assessment, board approval and regulator notification receipt retained 7 years after the individual leaves the position, under restricted access as personal data

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Appointments effective before the pack completed, expired screening beyond its validity period, undeclared conflicts discovered later and missed re-attestations are logged with root cause and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off every adverse finding disposition, every appointment proceeding despite an open item, and the remediation of any late or missing regulator notification

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All appointments, re-appointments and departures of directors, officers, controllers and key function holders in the year, plus the full population of in-scope individuals subject to the annual re-attestation

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any appointment effective before a completed and signed-off screening pack is a fail, as is any missed BMA notification; 100% annual re-attestation completion by 31 January; any conflict discovered outside the register is a fail escalated to the Nomination and Governance Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per appointment with an annual attestation cycle; testing runs quarterly over that quarter's appointments and departures, and annually in February over the completed attestation campaign and the conflicts register

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside HR, Legal and the secretariat and must not have performed screening on, or approved, any sampled appointment

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly fitness and propriety test workpaper (appointment population, pack completeness matrix, search re-performance, notification recomputation, conflicts reconciliation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Insurance Code of Conduct / corporate governance, with restricted access

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-individual fitness file with the screening pack, declarations, board approval and notification receipt, plus the conflicts register extract, producible for a BMA fitness review within 5 business days under restricted handling

Regulator response path.value: General Counsel is the named contact for BMA fitness and propriety enquiries; Corporate Secretary submits the notification and any supplementary information; the board chair is briefed before any adverse finding on a sitting director is disclosed

checklist.step: Maintain the list of positions in scope for a fitness assessment
actions: List every position the Code and the Insurance Act treat as an officer, controller or key function holder — board directors, CEO, CFO, chief risk, chief compliance, chief audit, chief actuary and the appointed actuary.
Tag each of those positions in the HRIS job profile so the appointment workflow cannot be started without triggering the fitness pack.
Review the list whenever the organisational structure changes and at least annually with the Nomination and Governance Committee.
Record the review date and the approving committee reference on the list.
checklist.done: every in-scope position is tagged in the HRIS job profile and the list carries a dated committee-approved review.

checklist.step: Trigger the assessment at nomination or offer, before any effective date is set
actions: Open the appointment workflow as soon as a candidate is nominated or an offer is extended for a tagged position.
Enter the proposed effective date and let the workflow compute the pack completion deadline as effective date minus 10 business days.
Notify the General Counsel and the Corporate Secretary the same day so the conflicts and notification steps start in parallel.
Block the HRIS hire or appointment event from being finalised while any pack item is outstanding.
checklist.done: the workflow is open with a computed pack deadline 10 business days before the effective date, and the appointment event is blocked until complete.

checklist.step: Collect the candidate's declaration pack
actions: Issue the pack for signature: current curriculum vitae, personal questionnaire, declaration of criminal convictions and regulatory action, declaration of bankruptcy or insolvency involvement, directorships held and other business interests.
Require an explicit statement of any relationship with a policyholder, supplier, reinsurer, broker or competitor of the group.
Capture the signature with the e-signature audit certificate showing signer identity and timestamp.
Return incomplete declarations for completion rather than accepting blanks — an unanswered question is not a negative answer.
checklist.done: a signed declaration pack with an audit certificate is on file, with no unanswered question in it.

checklist.step: Verify identity, right to work and stated qualifications
actions: Verify photographic identity and right to work in the jurisdiction of appointment and record the document type, number and expiry.
Verify each professional qualification claimed directly with the awarding body — actuarial fellowship, accountancy membership, legal admission — and record the verification reference.
Check for any disciplinary finding held by that professional body against the individual.
Attach every verification result to the fitness file with its run date.
checklist.done: identity, right to work and every claimed qualification are independently verified with references and run dates on file.

checklist.step: Run criminal, credit and insolvency background checks
actions: Order the background package covering criminal record, credit history, bankruptcy and insolvency, civil judgments and directorship disqualification for every jurisdiction the individual has lived or worked in over the past ten years.
Confirm the candidate's written consent to each check is on file before ordering.
Read the returned report rather than the vendor's headline status — a 'review' status with an unexplained judgment is not a pass.
Record the vendor reference, the run date and the validity period of each check.
checklist.done: consented multi-jurisdiction background checks are returned, read in full, and recorded with reference, run date and validity period.

checklist.step: Search the regulatory and disqualification registers
actions: Search the relevant regulator registers and enforcement databases for the individual's name and known aliases, covering insurance, securities and banking regulators in each jurisdiction of prior employment.
Search the producer licensing record where the individual has ever held an insurance licence and read any administrative action attached to it.
Search the company registries for current and past directorships and check whether any of those companies entered insolvency while the individual served.
Save the search screens with the search terms and dates — a later 'we checked' assertion is not evidence.
checklist.done: regulator, licensing and company registry searches are saved with search terms and dates for the individual and known aliases.

checklist.step: Screen against sanctions, PEP and adverse media lists
actions: Screen the individual and their known close associates against the consolidated sanctions lists, PEP lists and adverse media sources.
Adjudicate every hit as true or false with a written rationale and the identifiers used to discount a false positive — date of birth, nationality, middle name.
Escalate any true hit or unresolved partial match to the Financial Crime AML Officer and the General Counsel the same day.
Record the screening date and set a re-screen cycle for the duration of the appointment.
checklist.done: the individual and close associates are screened, every hit is adjudicated in writing, and an ongoing re-screen cycle is set.

checklist.step: Take and document references covering the whole employment history
actions: Obtain references from the two most recent regulated employers covering role, dates, and whether any disciplinary or fitness concern arose.
Reconcile the reference dates to the declared employment history and challenge every gap longer than three months with the candidate in writing.
Record who gave each reference, their role and the date given.
Treat a refused or vague reference from a regulated employer as an adverse indicator to be escalated, not an administrative inconvenience.
checklist.done: references cover the recent regulated employers, every employment gap over three months is explained in writing, and refusals are escalated.

checklist.step: Capture the conflicts declaration and enter it in the register
actions: Enter each declared interest in the conflicts register: the interest, the counterparty, the nature of the relationship, the date declared and whether it is actual or potential.
Determine the treatment for each — no action, recusal from specified decisions, divestment, or a bar on the appointment — and record who decided it.
Cross-check declared directorships against the group's supplier, broker, reinsurer and investment counterparty lists rather than relying on the individual to spot the overlap.
Publish the register to the Nomination and Governance Committee at each meeting.
checklist.done: every declared interest is on the register with a decided treatment and a cross-check against group counterparty lists.

checklist.step: Assess competence against the role's requirements and the board skills matrix
actions: Map the candidate's experience to the role's required competencies and, for directors, to the gaps identified in the board skills matrix.
For key function holders, evidence the technical qualification the function demands — an actuarial function head without the relevant qualification is not fit for that function.
Record where the candidate is developing rather than proficient and the support that will close it, with a review date.
Write a competence conclusion that stands on its own without the interview panel present.
checklist.done: a written competence conclusion maps experience to the role requirements and names any development gap with a review date.

checklist.step: Escalate adverse findings to General Counsel before the appointment proceeds
actions: Review every adverse or ambiguous finding: an unspent conviction, a regulatory action, an insolvency, an unresolved sanctions match or a refused reference.
Obtain the candidate's written explanation and weigh it against the finding rather than accepting it at face value.
Decide proceed, proceed with conditions, or decline, and write the reasoning into the fitness file.
Where the appointment proceeds despite a finding, record the mitigating conditions and inform the Nomination and Governance Committee before the appointment is made.
checklist.done: every adverse finding has a written General Counsel decision with reasoning, and any conditional appointment is disclosed to the committee first.

checklist.step: Obtain board or committee approval before the effective date
actions: Table the appointment paper with the completed fitness summary, the conflicts treatment and the competence conclusion.
Record the approving resolution with the appointment effective date and any conditions attached.
Confirm the resolution date pre-dates the effective date — approving an appointment already in effect does not cure it.
Update the statutory registers and the board portal membership on approval.
checklist.done: a dated approving resolution pre-dating the effective date is minuted, with conditions recorded and registers updated.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA of the appointment or departure within the statutory window
actions: Prepare the notification with the individual's details, the position, the effective date and confirmation that the fitness assessment was completed before that date.
Compute the deadline from the effective date under the Insurance Act notification window and load it into the filing calendar.
Submit through the BMA's electronic filing channel and capture the receipt against the individual's fitness file.
File a departure notification on the same basis when an officer or controller leaves, including where the departure follows a fitness concern.
checklist.done: every appointment and departure is notified inside the statutory window with the receipt filed against the individual's record.

checklist.step: Run the annual re-attestation of continuing fitness and conflicts
actions: Launch the attestation campaign on 2 January to every in-scope individual, asking them to confirm or update convictions, regulatory actions, insolvency, directorships and conflicts, with a 31 January due date.
Re-run sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening on the whole in-scope population in the same window and adjudicate hits.
Refresh credit and disqualification checks for anyone whose prior check has passed its validity period.
Escalate every changed answer to the General Counsel within 5 business days of receipt.
checklist.done: 100% of in-scope individuals attest by 31 January, screening is re-run, and every changed answer reaches General Counsel within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Retain the fitness files under restricted access
actions: Archive each individual's fitness file with the declarations, search results and run dates, references, competence conclusion, board resolution and notification receipt.
Apply the retention label of 7 years from the date the individual leaves the position and mark the record as personal data with restricted access.
Limit access to HR, Legal, the secretariat and Internal Audit and record the access list.
Confirm retrieval by individual, position and appointment date for a BMA fitness request.
checklist.done: each fitness file is archived under a 7-year post-departure label with restricted, recorded access and is retrievable by individual and position.

testing.step: Build the population of appointments, departures and in-scope individuals
actions: Extract every appointment, re-appointment and departure in the period for tagged positions with effective dates.
Extract the current in-scope population subject to the annual attestation.
Add the board minutes' record of appointments and the statutory registers so an appointment made outside the HRIS workflow is still captured.
Have the extractor sign the extract with queries, run date and counts.
testing.done: a signed population covers HRIS appointments, board-minuted appointments and the attestation population for the period.

testing.step: Reconcile the appointment population across HRIS, minutes and the registers
actions: Match each HRIS appointment to a board or committee resolution and to a statutory register entry.
List every resolution with no HRIS workflow — those are the appointments most likely to have skipped screening.
List every register entry with no resolution and query it with the Corporate Secretary.
Document every difference before sampling.
testing.done: appointments reconcile across HRIS, resolutions and registers, with every unmatched item documented and queried.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of appointments and attestations
actions: Take 100% of director, controller and key function holder appointments and departures in the period.
Take 20 attestation respondents at random with a recorded seed, plus 100% of respondents who reported a changed answer.
Take 100% of appointments where an adverse finding was recorded.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all officer appointments and adverse-finding cases plus a seeded attestation sample.

testing.step: Test pack completeness and that every item pre-dates the effective date
actions: Build a completeness matrix per sampled appointment: declaration, identity, qualification verification, background checks, register searches, sanctions screening, references, conflicts entry, competence conclusion, board resolution.
Read the run date on each item and compare it to the appointment effective date — an item dated after the effective date is a fail even if the result was clean.
Confirm no search result was beyond its validity period at the effective date.
Record a per-item pass or fail rather than an overall judgement.
testing.done: each sampled appointment has an item-by-item completeness matrix with every run date compared to the effective date.

testing.step: Re-perform the register and sanctions searches independently
actions: Re-run the sanctions, PEP and adverse media screen for 10 sampled individuals using the same name and alias set.
Re-run the regulator and company registry searches yourself and compare the hit set to the one on file.
Where the file shows a hit discounted as a false positive, re-read the rationale and confirm the discriminating identifier actually discriminates.
Capture your search screens with terms and dates into the workpaper.
testing.done: 10 individuals are independently re-screened with hit sets compared and every false-positive rationale re-tested.

testing.step: Recompute the BMA notification deadlines and trace the receipts
actions: For each appointment and departure recompute the notification deadline from the effective date under the Insurance Act window.
Compare to the actual submission date and quantify days late where applicable.
Open each filed receipt and confirm it names the individual, the position and the effective date reported.
Treat a departure with no notification as a fail equal in weight to a missing appointment notification.
testing.done: every appointment and departure has a hand-recomputed notification deadline, a days-late figure and an inspected receipt.

testing.step: Test the conflicts register for completeness against independent sources
actions: Take the register and compare declared directorships to a company registry search for each sampled individual.
Compare declared relationships to the group's supplier, broker, reinsurer and investment counterparty master lists.
Match conflicts declared in board minutes during the year to register entries and list any declared in a meeting but never registered.
Confirm each register entry shows a decided treatment and, where recusal was required, that the minutes show it happened.
testing.done: the register reconciles to registry searches, counterparty lists and meeting declarations, with every treatment traced to a minuted action.

testing.step: Test the annual attestation completion and follow-up on changed answers
actions: Compute the attestation completion rate against the 100% threshold at 31 January and list every non-responder with days late.
For every changed answer, trace the escalation to General Counsel and read the recorded decision and its date.
Confirm the periodic re-screening and refreshed checks were performed across the whole in-scope population, not only the new joiners.
List any individual whose prior check is past its validity period with no refresh.
testing.done: the completion rate is computed against 100%, every changed answer traces to a dated decision, and expired checks are listed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the individual reference, the position, the missing item or the days late, and the governance impact.
Assign a root cause: workflow bypassed, effective date brought forward, vendor turnaround, conflicts not cross-checked, or attestation not chased.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for any appointment made without a completed pack require a retrospective full screening within 30 days.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date, and incomplete appointments carry a 30-day retrospective screening requirement.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the result against the zero-tolerance thresholds: appointments effective before pack completion, missed notifications, unregistered conflicts and attestation completion percentage.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references behind each element.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside HR, Legal and the secretariat and screened no sampled individual, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Nomination and Governance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under restricted access.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with per-threshold results, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository under restricted access.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Board Governance Lead owns the policy inventory and the annual review schedule; each policy has a named executive owner, and the board itself approves the governance policy set on the Nomination and Governance Committee's recommendation

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Bermuda Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) s.5 (Corporate Governance) requiring documented governance policies and s.6 (Risk Management), read with the Insurance Sector Operational Cyber Risk Management Code of Conduct (2020) governance paragraph for the cyber policy set; all re-read before the annual review cycle opens

In-scope processes.value: The board-approved governance policy set — corporate governance framework, risk management and risk appetite, compliance, internal audit charter, conduct and fair treatment, conflicts of interest, outsourcing, information security and cyber, business continuity, data privacy and remuneration — from drafting through challenge, approval, publication and staff attestation

In-scope systems.value: Policy inventory, owner, version, review dates and Code mapping held in the GRC platform; approved versions published to the intranet and the board record held in the board portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: Governance Policy Lifecycle Procedure — inventory maintenance, Code mapping, annual review, second-line challenge, legal review, committee pre-review, board approval, publication, attestation, waiver handling and archiving

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the board and reviewed annually alongside the policy set; re-approved on any change to the Code or to the committee structure that owns a policy

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual cycle — review schedule published in January, owner drafts due 8 weeks before the approving meeting, second-line and legal review 4 weeks before, committee pre-review 2 weeks before, board approval within 12 months of the previous approval date; interim updates for regulatory change approved within 90 days of the change taking effect

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform notifications to the policy owner at 120, 90, 60 and 30 days before the review-due date, with an escalation to the Head of Compliance at 30 days and to the committee chair once a policy passes its 12-month anniversary

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each approved policy version, the change log, the second-line challenge note, the legal review, the board resolution and the attestation results retained 10 years, with superseded versions archived rather than deleted

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Policies past their 12-month review anniversary, approvals without a recorded resolution, published versions differing from the approved version and incomplete attestation campaigns are logged with root cause and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off the closure of every overdue-policy exception and every waiver granted against a governance policy before it is reported as resolved

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of governance policies approved within 12 months of their previous approval — any policy past its anniversary is a fail; the published version must match the approved version byte for byte; ≥98% staff attestation completion for policies requiring it; any Code obligation with no owning policy is a fail escalated to the board

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual policy governance test workpaper (inventory extract, Code coverage mapping, ageing recomputation, resolution trace, published-version comparison, attestation results, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Insurance Code of Conduct / corporate governance

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Policy inventory with owners, versions and approval dates, the approved policy PDFs, the Code coverage mapping and the board resolutions, producible for a BMA governance review within 5 business days
