checklist.step: Maintain the governance policy inventory as the single list of record
actions: Hold one row per policy: title, executive owner, approving body, current version, approval date, review-due date, publication location and retention class.

Include every governance-level policy — corporate governance framework, risk management and appetite, compliance, internal audit charter, conduct and fair treatment, conflicts, outsourcing, information security and cyber, business continuity, privacy and remuneration.
Remove nothing without a recorded board or committee decision to retire it, and archive the retired version rather than deleting the row.
Reconcile the inventory to the intranet policy library quarterly so an unlisted published policy is found.
checklist.done: the inventory holds a complete row per governance policy with owner, version and dates, reconciled quarterly to the published library.

checklist.step: Map every Code obligation to the policy that owns it
actions: List the governance obligations in s.5 and s.6 of the Bermuda Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) and the governance paragraph of the Cyber Code (2020).
Link each obligation in the GRC authority document to the policy clause that discharges it, quoting the clause text on the link.
List every obligation with no owning policy clause and raise it as a framework gap for the Nomination and Governance Committee.
Refresh the mapping whenever a policy is amended so the link points at the current clause, not a deleted one.
checklist.done: every Code governance obligation links to a quoted policy clause, and every unmapped obligation is raised as a framework gap.

checklist.step: Publish the annual review schedule in January
actions: Set each policy's review-due date at 12 months from its last approval date and assign it to a specific board or committee meeting on the year's calendar.
Work backwards to the owner's draft deadline at 8 weeks, second-line and legal review at 4 weeks and committee pre-review at 2 weeks before that meeting.
Spread the reviews across the calendar so no single meeting carries more policies than it can genuinely challenge.
Issue the schedule to every policy owner with their dates and confirm receipt.
checklist.done: a January-issued schedule assigns every policy to a meeting with owner, review and pre-review deadlines confirmed by each owner.

checklist.step: Have the owner draft the revision with a substantive change log
actions: Ask each owner to produce a redline against the approved version and a change log stating what changed, why, and which regulatory or business driver caused it.
Require an explicit statement where nothing changed — 'reviewed, no change required' with the owner's name and date is a valid outcome, silence is not.
Check the policy still names the accountable role, the escalation route and the consequence of non-compliance.
Return drafts that renumber clauses without explanation, since the Code mapping links to clause numbers.
checklist.done: each policy has a redline, a reasoned change log, or an explicit dated no-change statement from its owner.

checklist.step: Put the draft through second-line challenge
actions: Challenge whether the policy's requirements are actually operable — a control the business cannot perform is a policy that will be breached from day one.
Check the risk appetite statements in the policy are consistent with the board's approved appetite and with the limits in the risk register.
Check the cyber and outsourcing policies describe the three lines of defence in terms matching the Cyber Code's governance expectation.
Record the challenge and the owner's response in writing on the draft, including challenges the owner rejected.
checklist.done: a written second-line challenge and owner response sits with the draft, including rejected challenges and their reasons.

checklist.step: Obtain legal review of the drafted policy
actions: Check every regulatory reference and statutory citation in the policy is current and correctly quoted.
Check the policy does not create obligations broader than the regulator requires without the board knowingly accepting them.
Check consistency with the other policies in the set, particularly where conflicts, privacy and conduct overlap.
Record legal clearance with the version number and clearance date on the draft.
checklist.done: legal clearance is recorded against a version number with citations verified and cross-policy consistency checked.

checklist.step: Pre-review at the owning committee before the board sees it
actions: Table the draft at the owning committee with the redline, the change log, the second-line challenge and the legal clearance.
Minute the committee's substantive comments and the owner's undertakings, not merely that the paper was received.
Where the committee requires changes, re-issue the draft before board submission rather than presenting the board an amended-in-the-room version.
Record the committee's recommendation to the board with its date.
checklist.done: the owning committee's minuted comments and dated recommendation accompany the draft to the board.

checklist.step: Obtain board approval and record the resolution
actions: Table the final version in the board pack at least 5 business days before the meeting with the committee recommendation attached.
Minute the resolution naming the policy title, the version number approved and the effective date.
Confirm the approval date falls within 12 months of the previous approval date and note it in the minute where it does not.
Update the GRC inventory with the new version, approval date and the next review-due date the same week.
checklist.done: a resolution naming policy, version and effective date is minuted and the GRC inventory is updated within the week.

checklist.step: Publish the approved version and withdraw the superseded one
actions: Publish the approved PDF to the intranet policy library with the version number and effective date on the cover page.
Remove the superseded version from the live library the same day and move it to the archive with its own retention label.
Verify the published file matches the approved file by comparing checksums or version properties — a late editorial fix after approval is an unapproved policy.
Update every internal link and any procedure that cites the old version number.
checklist.done: the approved version is live, the superseded version is archived the same day, and the published file is verified identical to the approved file.

checklist.step: Run the staff attestation campaign for the policies that require one
actions: Identify the policies requiring individual attestation — conduct and fair treatment, conflicts, information security, privacy — and the audience for each.
Launch the attestation with a 30-day completion window and reminders at day 7, 21 and 28.
Track completion by department and escalate below-target departments to their head at day 21.
Record the attestation result per employee with the policy version attested, so a later attestation to an old version is visible.
checklist.done: attestation runs with a 30-day window and reminders, and each record names the employee and the exact policy version attested.

checklist.step: Operate the waiver and exception route rather than tolerating quiet breaches
actions: Require any departure from a governance policy to be raised as a waiver request with the business reason, the compensating control and an expiry date.
Approve at the level the policy specifies and never above a 12-month expiry without re-approval.
Maintain the waiver register and report open waivers to the owning committee at each meeting.
Treat a recurring waiver as evidence the policy is wrong and trigger an out-of-cycle policy review.
checklist.done: every departure is an approved, expiring waiver on the register, reported to committee, with recurring waivers triggering a policy review.

checklist.step: Handle regulatory change with an out-of-cycle update inside 90 days
actions: Monitor BMA publications and industry notices for amendments to the Insurance Code of Conduct and the Cyber Code and log each with its effective date.
Assess which policies the change touches using the Code-to-policy mapping and notify each affected owner within 5 business days.
Set the amended policy's approval deadline at 90 days from the change taking effect and schedule it into the next available meeting.
Record the assessment even where no policy change is needed, with the reasoning.
checklist.done: each regulatory change is logged, mapped to affected policies within 5 business days, and approved or reasoned away within 90 days.

checklist.step: Track overdue policies and escalate before the anniversary passes
actions: Refresh a monthly ageing view showing days to review-due date per policy, colour-coded at 60, 30 and 0 days.
Chase owners at 60 and 30 days in writing with the assigned meeting date restated.
Escalate any policy within 30 days of its 12-month anniversary to the Head of Compliance, and any that passes it to the committee chair the same week.
Record the escalation date and the recovery plan against the inventory row.
checklist.done: a monthly ageing view drives written chases at 60 and 30 days, with every anniversary breach escalated to the chair within the week.

checklist.step: Report policy framework health to the board quarterly
actions: Prepare the quarterly paper: policies in the inventory, approved in the quarter, due next quarter, overdue with days overdue, open waivers and any Code obligation with no owning policy.
State the percentage approved within 12 months against the 100% standard rather than describing it narratively.
Upload to the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting.
Minute the board's direction and carry any directed action into the inventory with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: a quarterly paper reports the 12-month approval percentage, overdue days and framework gaps, with directed actions tracked.

checklist.step: Archive superseded versions for the retention period
actions: Archive each superseded version with its change log, second-line challenge, legal clearance and the approving resolution reference.
Apply the 10-year retention label from the date the version was superseded so the company can show which policy applied on any past date.
Confirm retrieval by policy title, version and effective date range.
Record the archive completion against the inventory row.
checklist.done: each superseded version is archived with its full approval trail under a 10-year label and is retrievable by effective date range.

testing.step: Build the policy population from the inventory and the published library
actions: Extract the full policy inventory at period end with title, owner, approving body, version, approval date, review-due date and publication location.
Extract separately the intranet policy library listing, so a published policy missing from the inventory is visible.
Extract every board and committee resolution in the year that approved a policy.
Have the extractor sign each extract with query, run date and counts.
testing.done: signed extracts cover the inventory, the published library and the year's approving resolutions.

testing.step: Reconcile the inventory to the published library and to the Code obligations
actions: Match inventory rows to published documents and list every published policy with no inventory row and every inventory row with no published document.
Independently list the governance obligations in Code s.5 and s.6 and the Cyber Code governance paragraph and match each to an owning policy clause.
List every obligation with no owning policy — a framework gap is a fail regardless of how current the existing policies are.
Document every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the inventory reconciles to the published library and every Code governance obligation maps to an owning policy or is listed as a gap.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample of policies
actions: Take 100% of the policies the Code names directly — corporate governance framework, risk management, compliance, internal audit charter, conflicts and information security.
Take 10 further policies at random with a recorded seed from the remaining inventory.
Take 100% of policies approved out of cycle following a regulatory change.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers every Code-named policy and out-of-cycle approval plus a seeded random selection.

testing.step: Recompute the 12-month review ageing across the whole inventory
actions: For every policy compute days between the previous approval date and the current approval date and flag anything above 365 days.
For policies not yet re-approved, compute days elapsed since the last approval to period end and flag anything above 365.
Compute the percentage approved within 12 months against the 100% standard.
Quantify days overdue per breach rather than reporting a count alone.
testing.done: inventory-wide ageing is hand-recomputed with the 12-month percentage and days overdue quantified per breach.

testing.step: Trace each sampled approval to a board or committee resolution
actions: Open the minutes of the meeting the inventory names and read the resolution.
Confirm the resolution names the policy title, the version approved and the effective date — a minute reading 'policies were approved' does not evidence approval of a specific version.
Confirm the approving body is the one the charter assigns the policy to.
Confirm the pack containing the policy was distributed at least 5 business days before that meeting.
testing.done: each sampled approval traces to a resolution naming policy, version and effective date, taken by the charter-assigned body.

testing.step: Compare the published version to the approved version
actions: Download the published PDF and the board-approved PDF for each sampled policy.
Compare version number, effective date and content — checksum where possible, otherwise a page-by-page diff of the substantive clauses.
Confirm the superseded version is no longer reachable in the live library.
Any content difference is a fail, since staff are following a document the board did not approve.
testing.done: each sampled published document is proven identical to the approved version and no superseded version remains live.

testing.step: Re-perform the second-line challenge and legal review evidence check
actions: For each sampled policy locate the written second-line challenge and the owner's response, including rejected challenges.
Locate the legal clearance and confirm it names the version number that was ultimately approved, not an earlier draft.
Read the change log and confirm it explains the substantive changes visible in the redline — an unexplained clause deletion is an exception.
List any policy approved with no evidenced challenge or clearance.
testing.done: each sampled policy shows a written challenge, an owner response and a legal clearance naming the approved version.

testing.step: Test attestation completion and waiver discipline
actions: Compute attestation completion per policy against the 98% threshold and list non-completers by department.
Confirm each attestation record names the version attested and that it is the current approved version.
Take the waiver register and confirm each waiver has an approval at the level the policy specifies, an expiry inside 12 months and a compensating control.
List expired waivers still relied on and any recurring waiver with no triggered policy review.
testing.done: attestation completion is computed against 98% with version accuracy checked, and every waiver is tested for approval level, expiry and compensating control.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the policy, the owner, the days overdue or the specific deficiency.
Assign a root cause: owner capacity, meeting agenda congestion, challenge not performed, publication error, or framework gap.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for any policy past its anniversary require approval at the next available meeting.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly ageing check as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a next-meeting approval commitment where overdue.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the result against each threshold: percentage approved within 12 months, published-versus-approved differences, attestation completion and Code obligations with no owning policy.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references behind each element.
Have the reviewer, who owns no policy in the inventory and approved none of the sampled versions, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Nomination and Governance Committee and the board at their next sittings and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with per-threshold results, a stated conclusion and board reporting dates exists in the repository.
